A big cloud came and it started to rain and was very dark. The bird was scared, so it hid inside the birdcage.
But then after a while the noise stopped, and the sun came out and started to shine again. The bird was happy and could spread joy again.
The moral of the story is that bad times don't last. The sun will always shine again.

Mum and Dad took Anna to an interesting place. All around were big trees, long grass and rocks. They stopped the jeep and Mum said "We want to let you experience something special."
Anna looked around in excitement. Then she saw it. A little parade of animals coming through the long grass. Anna was so excited, she asked "Why are those animals here? Can I play with them?"
Mum smiled and said "No, Anna, these animals are wild. The law doesn't permit us to play with them. But you can look, and watch if you like."
So Anna watched the wild animals. She saw squirrels, birds and even a fox. It was so interesting to watch them go by, each one looking different and strange.
Eventually, Mum and Dad said it was time to go home. They all climbed back into the jeep and drove away, but Anna would never forget her special experience of watching the wild animals.

They went to the forest and began looking around. Everywhere they looked, the forest seemed quiet and sad. They began to feel a bit sad too. 
Suddenly, an old owl flew down from the branches above and sat right in front of them. "Hello," the owl said, "I can help you. I can take you on a real tour of the forest."
Dave and Jo were very excited and they accepted the offer. The owl flew gracefully through the trees, showing them all the different plants and animals in the forest. 
As they looked around they noticed that the sadness in the forest was slowly fading away, replaced by joy and laughter. 
Dave and Jo realized that the owl had given them a very special gift. By taking them on a tour of the forest, the owl had brightened the spirits of everyone in the forest.

"Well, it keeps me warm and it's very comforting," she answered with a smile. 
The grandkids weren't convinced yet, but Grandma knew what she was doing. 
The next morning, the grandkids awoke to the smell of cookies coming from the kitchen. There was Grandma, wearing her bathrobe, baking up a batch of cookies just for them.

Once upon a time there was a leaf who was enthusiastic about life. Every day the leaf worked hard to tilt with the wind and flutter around the trees. One day the leaf encountered a big gust of wind and far away it could see a darker tree.
The leaf was so entusiastic that it wanted to see what was over there. So it kept on working hard and as it fluttered towards the darker tree it watched the darkness getting closer.
The leaf reached the tree and spoke, "Hello, what is 10 feet away from here?" The tree was silent and the leaf fluttered away.
Suddenly the leaf heard a deep voice roar, "Behind you!" It quickly turned around and there the leaf saw a large river lying between it and the tree. The leaf became scared, for the river seemed too wide to swim across.
The leaf worked hard by jumping and fluttering and gradually managed to reach the other side. When it went back to the tree, the leaf asked, "What is going to happen now?"
The tree spoke again in a deep voice, "Remember, if you're too entusiastic, you can miss out on what is right behind you." The lesson the leaf learnt was that it is important to understand and observe the situation before taking off.

Now, everywhere Brody went, he took the fabric and wrapped his brain. He shared the power with his family and friends, and they all learned to use their brains in amazing ways. Brody was bald, but his brain was now the wisest one around.

From that day on, the monkey and the elephant became the best of friends in the zoo. They played together and shared their food. And the zookeeper never forgot to supply the monkey with bananas again!

Tom and Lily say, "Yes, Mom, we can do that." They put on their helmets and backpacks and ride their bikes to the store. They see many things on the way. They see cars and trucks and buses. They see dogs and cats and birds. They see flowers and trees and grass.
They get to the store and park their bikes. They go inside and find the milk and eggs. They pay the lady and put them in their backpacks. They say, "Thank you, lady, have a nice day."
They ride their bikes back home. They see more things on the way. They see a big hill and decide to go up. They pedal hard and reach the top. They see the whole town and the sky and the sun. They say, "Wow, this is amazing. We are so high."
They go down the hill and feel the wind in their faces. They laugh and shout, "Whee, this is fun. We are so fast."
They get home and give the milk and eggs to Mom. Mom says, "Thank you, Tom and Lily, you did a great job. You are very good riders. I am proud of you."
Tom and Lily say, "You're welcome, Mom, we are happy to help. We had a lot of fun. We saw many things. We went up a big hill and it was amazing."
Mom says, "That sounds wonderful. I'm glad you enjoyed your ride. Now, let's have some dinner. I made your favorite, mac and cheese."
Tom and Lily say, "Yay, we love mac and cheese. Thank you, Mom, you are the best."
They hug Mom and sit down to eat. They tell Mom more about their ride and their task. They are hungry and happy. They love their bikes and their Mom.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to eat fruit. One day, their mom gave them a big bowl of strawberries to share. Sara was happy and said, "Thank you, mom! I love strawberries!" Tom was not happy and said, "I don't want strawberries. I want cookies!"
Mom said, "You can have cookies later, Tom. Now you have to eat some strawberries. They are good for you and they taste sweet."
Tom did not listen to mom. He picked a strawberry and bit it. He made a face and said, "Yuck! This strawberry is bitter! It is not sweet at all!"
Sara looked at Tom and said, "You are silly, Tom. That is not a strawberry. That is a lemon. You picked the wrong fruit. Look, this is a strawberry. It is red and soft and juicy. Try it, it is yummy!"
Tom looked at the bowl and saw that Sara was right. He had picked a lemon by mistake. He felt silly and said, "Oops! I am sorry, mom. I did not see well. Can I have a strawberry, please?"
Mom smiled and said, "Of course, Tom. Here you go. And next time, don't complain before you try something new. You might like it."
Tom took a strawberry and bit it. He smiled and said, "You are right, mom. This strawberry is sweet and yummy. I like it. Thank you, mom!"
Sara and Tom ate their strawberries and enjoyed them. They did not complain anymore. They were happy and said, "We love strawberries!"

Lily and Tom were twins who loved to play with their puppy, Spot. Spot was a brown and white dog who liked to run, jump and lick their faces. One day, Lily and Tom decided to have a picnic in the garden with Spot. They packed some bread, cheese, apples and juice in a basket and spread a blanket on the grass.
"Spot, come here!" Lily called. "We have some yummy food for you!" She gave him a piece of cheese and a slice of apple. Spot wagged his tail and ate them happily.
"Can I have some juice, please?" Tom asked. He reached for the bottle in the basket, but Lily stopped him.
"No, Tom, this juice is mine!" she said. "You have your own juice over there!" She pointed to another bottle on the other side of the blanket.
"But I want this juice!" Tom said. "It looks better than mine!" He tried to grab the bottle from Lily, but she held it tight.
"Stop it, Tom, you're being mean!" Lily said. "This is my juice and you can't have it!"
They started to pull the bottle from each other, making it shake and spill. Spot watched them with his ears up, wondering what was going on.
Suddenly, the bottle popped open and the juice squirted out. It splashed on Lily and Tom's faces and clothes, making them wet and sticky. It also sprayed on Spot's nose, making him sneeze.
"Yuck!" Lily and Tom said at the same time. They tasted the juice on their lips and made a face. It was sour and bitter, not sweet and yummy like they thought.
"Spot, do you like this juice?" Lily asked, wiping her mouth.
Spot licked his nose and shook his head. He did not like the juice either. It made him feel funny.
"Sorry, Lily, I didn't know the juice was sour," Tom said, feeling bad.
"Sorry, Tom, I didn't mean to be mean," Lily said, feeling bad too.
They hugged each other and said they were sorry. They also hugged Spot and said they were sorry to him. They threw away the sour juice and shared the other bottle, which was good and fresh. They finished their picnic and played with Spot, who was happy again. They learned to not fight over things and to share with each other and their puppy.

Lila loved to play her flute. She liked the sound it made when she blew into it. She learned many songs from her mom and dad. They were proud of her and gave her hugs.
One day, Lila found a mysterious flute in the attic. It was shiny and had many colors. She wondered who it belonged to and how it got there. She picked it up and tried to play it.
But when she blew into it, nothing happened. No sound came out. She tried again and again, but still nothing. She felt sad and confused.
She heard a voice behind her. "That's my flute. You can't play it. It's magic."
Lila turned around and saw a fairy. She had wings and a dress and a crown. She looked angry and scared.
Lila was surprised and curious. She had never seen a fairy before. She wanted to be friends with her. She said, "I'm sorry. I didn't know it was yours. I like flutes. Can you show me how to play it?"
The fairy looked at Lila. She saw that she was not mean or greedy. She saw that she was kind and gentle. She felt sorry and happy.
She said, "It's okay. I forgive you. I can show you how to play it. But you have to keep it a secret. No one else can know about me or my flute. Do you promise?"
Lila nodded and smiled. She said, "I promise. I won't tell anyone. Can we be friends?"
The fairy nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, we can be friends. My name is Faye. What's yours?"
Lila said, "My name is Lila. I'm glad to meet you, Faye."
They hugged and laughed. They played the flute together. They made beautiful music. They became the best of friends.

Tim and Sam were playing outside with their toy cars. They liked to make them go fast and make loud noises. They saw a big cloud in the sky. It was white and fluffy, like cotton.
"Look, Tim, a cloud!" Sam said. "It looks like a bunny."
Tim looked up and smiled. "You're right, Sam. It does look like a bunny. Maybe it's hopping to find some carrots."
They watched the cloud for a while, until it changed shape. Now it looked like a dragon.
"Wow, Sam, a dragon!" Tim said. "It looks scary and strong. Maybe it's breathing fire."
Sam nodded. "You're right, Tim. It does look scary and strong. Maybe it's guarding a treasure."
They watched the cloud for a while, until it changed shape again. Now it looked like a flower.
"Look, Tim, a flower!" Sam said. "It looks pretty and sweet. Maybe it's smelling nice."
Tim shook his head. "No, Sam. It's not a flower. It's a dead flower. See, it has no color and no petals. Maybe it's sad and lonely."
Sam frowned. "You're right, Tim. It does look dead and sad. Maybe it needs some water and sun."
They felt sorry for the cloud. They wanted to help it.
"Let's clean the cloud, Tim," Sam said. "Maybe we can make it happy again."
Tim agreed. "Let's clean the cloud, Sam. Maybe we can make it white and fluffy again."
They ran inside and got a bucket and a sponge. They filled the bucket with water and soap. They ran outside and threw the water and soap at the cloud. They tried to scrub it with the sponge.
"Clean, clean, clean!" they shouted.
But the cloud did not change. It stayed dead and gray. It started to rain.
"Uh-oh, Tim," Sam said. "I think we made the cloud angry."
Tim nodded. "Uh-oh, Sam. I think we made the cloud cry."
They dropped the bucket and the sponge. They ran inside and hid under the bed.
They decided to never clean a cloud again.

"Hey, you soaked me!" said Ben.
"Sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to," said Lily.

Tim and Mia were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things on the beach, like shells, crabs, and birds. But they also saw something they did not like: jellyfish.
"Look, mom, jellyfish!" Tim said, pointing at the shiny blobs on the shore. "They are icky and stingy. Can we poke them with a stick?"
"No, Tim, you can't poke them with a stick," mom said. "They are alive, and they have value. They are part of the sea, and they have a job to do. They eat tiny things that we can't see, and they help keep the water clean. They also have feelings, and they don't like to be hurt."
"But they hurt us if we touch them," Mia said. "They have long tentacles that make us ouchy. How can we play in the water if they are there?"
"Sometimes, jellyfish come to the shore because of the wind and the waves," dad said. "But they don't stay there for long. They go back to the deep water when the tide changes. We just have to be patient and wait for them to leave. Then we can play in the water again. But we have to be careful and look where we step, and not touch them if we see them."
Tim and Mia nodded. They understood that jellyfish had value, even if they did not like them. They decided to play with their buckets and shovels and make a sandcastle instead. They were patient and waited for the jellyfish to go away. They hoped they would see some nice fish or dolphins instead. They loved the beach and all the things they could see and learn there.

Lily likes pears. She likes to eat them when they are ripe and sweet. She sees a big pear tree in the park. She wants to pick a pear, but the tree is too tall.
She sees a boy with a red bike. He is fast and can ride very well. She runs to him and asks, "Can you help me get a pear?"
The boy stops his bike and looks at her. He smiles and says, "Sure, I can help you. I have a ladder in my bike basket. Come with me."
They go to the pear tree. The boy puts the ladder against the trunk. He climbs up and picks a pear. He throws it to Lily. She catches it and says, "Thank you, thank you! You are very kind."
The boy climbs down and says, "You're welcome. Do you want to try my bike? It is fun and fast."
Lily nods and says, "Yes, please. I like bikes. Can you teach me how to ride?"
The boy says, "Of course. I will hold the bike for you. Don't be afraid. You can do it."
They take turns riding the bike and eating the pear. They have a good time and become friends. They share their names and stories. They like the same things. They are happy.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the garden. The garden has many flowers and trees and bugs. Lily and Ben like to smell the flowers and watch the bugs.
One day, they see a big butterfly. It has many colors on its wings. It flies from flower to flower. Lily and Ben want to catch it. They run after it with a net.
"Come here, butterfly!" Lily says. "We want to see you up close!"
But the butterfly is fast and smart. It flies away from the net. It goes to a tall tree. Lily and Ben cannot reach it.
"Aw, no!" Ben says. "We lost the butterfly!"
They are sad. They sit on the grass and look at the tree.
Then, they hear a voice. It is the butterfly. It says:
"Hello, Lily and Ben. Why do you want to catch me?"
Lily and Ben are surprised. They look up and see the butterfly on a branch.
"We want to see you up close," Lily says. "You are so pretty and colorful."
The butterfly says:
"Thank you, but I do not like to be caught. I like to be free and fly in the garden. The garden is my home. I have many friends here. The flowers and the trees and the bugs. They are good to me. They give me food and shelter and company. I am grateful for them."
Lily and Ben listen to the butterfly. They understand. They say:
"We are sorry, butterfly. We did not mean to scare you or hurt you. We just wanted to play with you. We like the garden too. It is fun and beautiful. We are grateful for it."
The butterfly says:
"It is okay, Lily and Ben. I forgive you. You are nice and curious. You can play with me, but not catch me. You can watch me and talk to me, but not touch me. Do you agree?"
Lily and Ben nod. They say:
"Yes, butterfly. We agree. We will be gentle and respectful. We will be your friends."
The butterfly smiles. It says:
"Thank you, Lily and Ben. You are smart and kind. You make me happy. Come, let us play in the garden. There is so much to see and learn and enjoy."
Lily and Ben smile too. They get up and follow the butterfly. They play in the garden. They are happy.

Anna was a big girl who liked to help her grandma. Grandma had a cane that she used to walk, because her legs were not strong. Sometimes, Anna wanted to hold the cane and pretend she was a pirate or a fairy.
One day, Anna and Grandma went to the park to feed the ducks. Anna saw a big stick on the ground and picked it up. She said, "Look, Grandma, I have a cane too! Can I have yours?"
Grandma smiled and said, "No, dear, I need my cane to walk. You can play with the stick, but please give me my cane."
But Anna did not listen. She said, "No, I want your cane! It is shiny and pretty and makes a nice sound. Please, please, please!"
She tried to pull the cane from Grandma's hand, but Grandma held it tight. Anna pulled harder and harder, until Grandma lost her balance and fell on the grass. She cried out in pain and dropped the cane.
Anna was scared. She saw Grandma lying on the ground, looking helpless and sad. She realized she had been very naughty and hurt Grandma. She dropped the stick and ran to Grandma. She said, "I'm sorry, Grandma, I'm sorry! Are you okay? Do you need help?"
Grandma was not badly hurt, but she was sore and angry. She said, "Anna, you were very selfish and rude. You did not listen to me and you made me fall. You could have broken my cane or my bones. How would you feel if I took something you needed and made you fall?"
Anna felt ashamed and sorry. She said, "I feel bad, Grandma, I feel very bad. I was just playing, I did not mean to hurt you. I love you, Grandma, and I love your cane. Can you forgive me?"
Grandma sighed and hugged Anna. She said, "I love you too, Anna, and I forgive you. But you have to learn to respect other people's things and needs. You can't always insist on having your way. Sometimes, you have to share and be kind. Do you understand?"
Anna nodded and said, "I understand, Grandma, I do. I will be a good girl and listen to you. Can we still feed the ducks?"
Grandma smiled and said, "Yes, we can. But first, let me get up and get my cane. And you can help me, okay?"
Anna said, "Okay, Grandma, I will help you. And I will never take your cane again. I promise."

Tom was a brave boy who liked to play with his toy sword. He pretended it was a weapon to fight bad guys and monsters. One night, he heard a loud noise outside his window. He grabbed his sword and went to see what it was.
He saw a big, hairy animal with sharp teeth and claws. It was a bear! The bear was looking for food in the trash cans. Tom was scared, but he did not run away. He shouted at the bear, "Go away, you are not welcome here!"
The bear heard Tom and turned to face him. It growled and showed its teeth. It was angry and hungry. It started to walk towards Tom, ready to attack. Tom held his sword in front of him. He hoped it would scare the bear away.
But the bear did not stop. It got closer and closer to Tom. Tom felt his heart beat fast. He did not know what to do. He wished his mom or dad would come and help him. He closed his eyes and prayed.
Then, he heard another noise. It was a loud bark. It was his dog, Rex. Rex was a big, hairy dog, but he was friendly and loyal. He loved Tom and wanted to protect him. He ran out of the house and jumped on the bear. He bit the bear's ear and pulled its fur. He barked and snarled.
The bear was surprised and hurt. It did not like Rex. It did not want to fight a dog. It decided to leave and find another place to eat. It ran away from Rex and Tom. It disappeared into the dark.
Tom opened his eyes and saw Rex. He was happy and relieved. He hugged Rex and thanked him. He said, "You are my hero, Rex. You saved me from the bear. You are the best dog ever!"
Rex licked Tom's face and wagged his tail. He was happy too. He had done his job. He had defended his friend. He barked and smiled.
Tom and Rex went back to the house. They found Tom's mom and dad. They told them what had happened. Tom's mom and dad were shocked and proud. They praised Tom and Rex. They said, "You are both very brave and smart. We are glad you are safe. We love you very much!"
Tom and Rex felt warm and cozy. They cuddled with Tom's mom and dad. They were a happy family. They went to bed and slept well. They dreamed of good things.

Sara loved to draw. She drew many things, like trees, flowers, and animals. She wanted to improve her drawing skills, so she practiced every day. She asked her mom and dad to help her and give her tips.
One day, she decided to draw a reindeer. She had seen a picture of a reindeer in a book, and she thought they looked cute and funny. She took her crayons and paper and started to draw. She drew a big head, a long nose, two ears, and two eyes. Then she drew a body, four legs, and a tail. She was happy with her drawing, but she felt something was missing.
She looked at the picture in the book again, and she saw that the reindeer had antlers on its head. She had forgotten to draw them. She took a brown crayon and tried to add them, but they looked messy and crooked. She was not happy with her drawing anymore. She showed it to her mom and asked, "Mom, how can I improve my reindeer drawing?"
Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Sara, your reindeer drawing is very good. You have drawn all the important parts, and you have used nice colors. But if you want to improve it, you can try to draw the antlers more carefully. You can use a pencil first, and then trace over it with a crayon. You can also look at how the antlers curve and branch in the picture, and try to copy that. Do you want to try again?"
Sara nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I want to try again. Thank you for helping me. You are very reliable. You always help me when I need it." She took a new paper and a pencil, and followed her mom's advice. She drew the reindeer again, and this time, she added the antlers with more detail and accuracy. She was very proud of her drawing, and she showed it to her dad. He said, "Wow, Sara, your reindeer drawing is amazing. You have improved a lot. You are a very talented artist. I love you." Sara smiled and said, "I love you too, dad. And I love drawing reindeer. They are very cute and funny." She hung her drawing on the fridge, and looked at it with joy.

Lily liked to play in her mom's closet. She liked to look at the pretty dresses and shoes and hats. Sometimes she tried them on and pretended to be a princess or a fairy. One day, she saw a new thing in the closet. It was a soft and fluffy bathrobe. It was pink and had shiny buttons and a belt. Lily thought it was very pretty and expensive. She wanted to try it on.
She took the bathrobe and put it on. It was too big for her, but she didn't mind. She wrapped it around her and tied the belt. She felt warm and cozy. She looked at herself in the mirror and smiled. She thought she looked like a queen. She decided to show her mom.
She walked out of the closet and went to find her mom. She saw her in the kitchen, making lunch. She said, "Mom, look at me! I'm a queen!"
Her mom turned around and saw her. She was surprised and angry. She said, "Lily, what are you doing? That's my new bathrobe! I just bought it for my birthday! It's very expensive and delicate! You can't play with it! You might ruin it!"
Lily felt sad and scared. She didn't know it was her mom's birthday present. She didn't mean to make her mom angry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know. I just wanted to try it on. It's so pretty and soft. I like it."
Her mom sighed and calmed down. She said, "I know, Lily. It is pretty and soft. But it's not a toy. It's a special thing for me. You have to ask me before you touch my things. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. Can I give you a hug?"
Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. I love you. Come here and give me a hug."
Lily took off the bathrobe and gave it back to her mom. Then she hugged her mom and said, "I love you too, mom. Happy birthday."
Her mom hugged her back and said, "Thank you, Lily. You're my sweet girl."

Tom and Lily liked to play pretend. They had a big box of old things that they used for their games. One day, they found a microphone in the box. It was shiny and black, and had a long wire.
"Let's play singers!" Lily said. She was bossy and always wanted to be the leader. She grabbed the microphone and held it to her mouth. "Hello, hello, I am Lily and I am the best singer in the world!"
Tom wanted to try the microphone too. He reached for it, but Lily pulled it away. "No, Tom, you can't have it. It's mine. You have to polish it for me. It's dirty and dusty. Go get a cloth and make it shiny."
Tom was sad and angry. He didn't want to polish the microphone. He wanted to sing with it. He thought Lily was being mean and selfish. He said, "No, Lily, that's not fair. You have to share. The microphone is for both of us. Let me have a turn."
Lily shook her head. She didn't want to share. She said, "No, Tom, you have to do what I say. I am the star and you are the helper. Now go polish the microphone or I won't play with you."
Tom didn't like that. He didn't want to be the helper. He wanted to be the star too. He said, "No, Lily, you are not the star. You are the bossy. You are not nice. I don't want to play with you. I will find another friend who will share with me."
Tom left the box and went to look for another toy. Lily was left alone with the microphone. She felt lonely and sorry. She realized that she had hurt Tom's feelings. She wished she had been nicer to him. She put down the microphone and ran after him. She said, "Tom, Tom, wait. I'm sorry. I was wrong. You can have the microphone. You can be the star too. Please come back and play with me."
Tom heard Lily's voice. He turned around and saw her face. She looked sad and sorry. He felt sorry for her too. He said, "Lily, Lily, it's okay. I forgive you. You can have the microphone. You can be the star too. Let's go back and play together."
Lily smiled and hugged Tom. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. I'm sorry I was bossy. Let's share the microphone and sing together."
Tom smiled and hugged Lily back. He said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are a good friend too. I'm sorry I was angry. Let's share the microphone and sing together."
They went back to the box and picked up the microphone. They held it together and sang a happy song. They had fun and forgot their fight. They learned to be kind and share. They were the best singers in the world.

Ben and Mia like to play with blocks. They make towers and bridges and houses with the blocks. They have many colors and shapes of blocks.
One day, they have a new game. They want to see who can make the highest stack of blocks. They each take some blocks and start to build. Ben puts a big block on the bottom and then some smaller blocks on top. Mia puts a small block on the bottom and then some bigger blocks on top.
"Look, my stack is higher than yours!" Mia says. She smiles and claps her hands.
"No, it is not!" Ben says. He frowns and pushes his stack a little higher.
"Yes, it is!" Mia says. She pushes her stack a little higher too.
They keep pushing their stacks higher and higher. They do not see that their stacks are not very stable. They are too busy trying to win.
Suddenly, Mia's stack falls over. The blocks crash to the floor and make a loud noise. Mia gasps and starts to cry.
"Oh no, my stack!" she says. She feels miserable.
Ben looks at his stack. It is still standing, but it is very wobbly. He feels sorry for Mia, but he also feels proud of his stack.
"I win, I win!" he says. He jumps up and down.
But then, his stack falls over too. The blocks crash to the floor and make another loud noise. Ben gasps and starts to cry.
"Oh no, my stack!" he says. He feels miserable too.
Mia and Ben look at each other. They see that they both have no stack. They see that they both have tears in their eyes. They see that they both have sad faces.
They feel bad for making each other miserable. They feel silly for fighting over the stacks. They feel sorry for breaking the blocks.
They hug each other and say sorry.
"Let's play together, not against each other," Mia says.
"OK, let's do that," Ben says.
They pick up the blocks and start to build again. They make a new game. They want to see who can make the heaviest stack of blocks. They weigh the blocks with their hands and put them in a big pile. They laugh and have fun. They are happy again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs under the rocks and in the grass. They had a jar to keep the bugs they found.
"Look, I found a big bug!" Tom said, holding up a shiny beetle. "It has a hard shell and six legs."
"Wow, can I see?" Lily asked, reaching for the bug. Tom gave it to her, but she held it too tight. The bug split in two and fell to the ground.
"Oops, I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to break your bug," Lily said, feeling sad.
"That's okay, Lily. It was an accident. Maybe we can find another bug," Tom said, trying to be nice.
They looked around and saw a small bug crawling on a flower. It was green and had wings. It looked mild and friendly.
"Look, there's another bug. Maybe we can catch it," Lily said, pointing to the bug.
"Okay, let's try. But be gentle, Lily. We don't want to hurt it," Tom said, nodding.
They crept closer to the bug, holding their jar. They waited for the right moment, then put the jar over the bug. They slid the lid on and smiled.
"Yay, we did it! We caught a bug!" they cheered, holding up their jar.
They looked at the bug and saw it was happy. It flew around in the jar and made a soft buzzing sound.
"Hello, bug. We are Tom and Lily. We are your friends," they said to the bug.
The bug seemed to understand. It buzzed back and smiled.
Tom and Lily were happy. They had a new bug friend. They decided to name it Buzz. They took Buzz inside and showed it to their mom. She said they could keep it, but they had to let it go outside sometimes. They agreed and thanked her.
They played with Buzz all day. They gave it some water and some flowers. They watched it fly and land. They listened to it buzz and talk. They had fun with their bug friend. They were glad they found it.

Tom and Sam like to play in the old farm. They find many things to see and touch. But they know some things are dangerous and they do not go near them.
One day, they see a big tank in the field. It is green and brown and has a long pipe. They wonder what it is and how it got there.
"Let's go and look at the tank," Tom says. He runs towards it.
"No, Tom, wait!" Sam says. He is scared. He remembers what his dad told him. "The tank is old and bad. It can rot and make you sick. It can also boom and hurt you. We should stay away from it."
But Tom does not listen. He climbs on the tank and tries to open the door. He pulls and pushes, but the door does not move. He kicks it hard.
Suddenly, the door falls off and a bad smell comes out. Tom screams and jumps off the tank. He sees something black and slimy inside. He feels sick and runs back to Sam.
"Sam, Sam, help me!" Tom cries. "The tank is full of rot. It is gross and scary. I want to go home."
Sam hugs Tom and tries to calm him down. He wipes his face and hands with a cloth. He says, "It's okay, Tom. You are safe now. Let's go home and tell dad what happened. He will know what to do. And next time, listen to me when I say something is dangerous, okay?"
Tom nods and says, "Okay, Sam. I'm sorry. You are a good friend. Let's go home."
They hold hands and walk away from the tank. They do not look back. They have learned their lesson.

"Can we go near the fountain, Mom?" Ben asked.
"Okay, but be careful. The water is wet and cold," Mom said.

"Look, Mom, I made a snake!" Ben said.
"Look, Mom, I made a star!" Lily said.
Mom smiled and took pictures. She was happy to see Ben and Lily have fun.
But then, the wind blew hard. The water spray changed direction. It went to Ben and Lily and Mom. They got wet all over. They gasped and shivered.
"Oops, the fountain got us!" Mom said.
Ben and Lily giggled. They did not mind being wet. They liked the fountain. They hugged Mom and thanked her for taking them to the park. They went home to change and have hot chocolate. They had a good Wednesday.

But there is something else in the box. There is a mask. The mask is black and shiny. It has feathers and jewels. It has holes for the eyes and the mouth. The mask is mysterious. Lila and Tom wonder who wore the mask. They wonder why they wore the mask.
Lila has an idea. She puts on the dress and the mask. She looks at herself in the mirror. She thinks she looks like a princess. She says to Tom, "Do you like my dress and my mask? Do you want to play with me?"
Tom nods. He thinks Lila looks like a princess too. He says to Lila, "Yes, I like your dress and your mask. They are very nice. I want to play with you. What do you want to do?"
Lila smiles. She says to Tom, "Let's pretend we are going to a ball. A ball is a party with music and dancing. We can dance in the attic. We can have fun."
Tom agrees. He says to Lila, "OK, let's pretend we are going to a ball. A ball sounds fun. We can dance in the attic. We can have fun."
Lila and Tom hold hands. They spin and twirl. They laugh and sing. They dance in the attic. They have fun. They do not hear their mom calling them for lunch. They do not see the dust and the cobwebs. They only see the dress and the mask. They only feel the velvet and the mystery. They only play.

Tom and Anna were twins who liked to go on journeys. They had a big map on their wall with many places to see. They were very organized and packed their bags with things they needed. They had a tent, a flashlight, a book, and some snacks.
One day, they decided to go on a journey to the park. They put on their hats and shoes and told their mom they were leaving. Their mom said, "Be careful and come back soon." They said, "OK, mom, bye!"
They walked to the park, holding hands and looking at the map. They saw many things on the way: a dog, a bike, a flower, a bird. They said hello to them and asked them questions. The dog barked, the bike rang, the flower smelled, the bird sang. They were very friendly and curious.
But when they got to the park, they saw a big boy who was not nice. He was playing with a ball and he kicked it hard at them. He said, "Go away, this is my park!" Tom and Anna were scared and sad. They did not want to play with him. They wanted to find a nice place to set up their tent and read their book.
They decided to ignore the big boy and his ball. They looked at their map and found a spot under a big tree. They walked there and set up their tent. They went inside and opened their book. They read about animals and adventures. They ate their snacks and smiled. They were happy and cozy.
The big boy saw them and got angry. He wanted to bother them and make them leave. He ran to their tent and tried to pull it down. He shouted, "Hey, you, get out of my park!" Tom and Anna heard him and felt scared and angry. They did not want to talk to him. They wanted to enjoy their journey.
They decided to ignore the big boy and his shouting. They closed their book and turned on their flashlight. They pretended they were in a cave and told each other stories. They made funny noises and laughed. They were brave and fun.
The big boy got tired and bored. He saw that Tom and Anna did not care about him and his ball. He felt lonely and sad. He wished he had someone to play with. He decided to leave them alone and find someone else. He picked up his ball and walked away. He said, "Fine, I don't need you anyway!"
Tom and Anna did not hear him and did not care. They were having a great time on their journey. They hugged each other and said, "We are the best twins ever!" They were happy and proud.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big pond with some ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them some bread. They walked to the edge of the pond and threw some bread in the water.
But then they saw something else in the pond. It was a big green crocodile with sharp teeth. It was swimming towards them. It looked hungry and angry.
"Look, Lila, a crocodile!" Tom said. "It wants to eat us!"
Lila was scared. She grabbed Tom's hand and ran away. But the crocodile was fast. It came out of the water and chased them.
"Help, help!" Lila and Tom shouted.
They saw a big slide nearby. They climbed up the ladder and slid down. The crocodile followed them. It also climbed up the ladder and slid down.
But Lila was smart. She had an idea. She saw a big stick on the ground. She picked it up and waited for the crocodile.
When the crocodile slid down, Lila pushed the stick in its mouth. The crocodile could not bite. It made a loud noise and shook its head.
"Ha, ha, take that, crocodile!" Lila said. "You can't eat us now!"
Lila and Tom ran to their mom and dad. They told them what happened. Their mom and dad hugged them and praised them.
"You are very brave and smart, Lila and Tom!" they said. "You saved yourselves from the crocodile!"
Lila and Tom smiled. They were happy and proud. They did not want to play near the pond anymore. They played on the swings and the seesaw instead. They had fun and forgot about the crocodile.

I think your journal is beautiful and amazing. You are a good writer and a good friend. Can I see your journal?"

Lily and Anna hugged and smiled. They sat down and started to write in their journals. They ignored Ben and his mean words. They knew they had something special and valuable. They had their journals and their friendship.

Sara and Ben nod and say sorry again. They go back to the park and play with their ball. They decide to never go near the kayak again.

They marched for what felt like hours, until finally the soldier stopped and shouted "Let's take a break!" The children were tired, but were happy to eat their healthy snacks that the soldier had given them.
After the break, the soldier thanked the children and yelled out "Let's go!"  Everyone cheered and they all marched back to their homes. 
The soldier said goodbye to the children, who waved goodbye and shouted "Thank you soldier!" He waved back and returned to his post.  The soldier knew that he had made a difference in the lives of these healthy children.

Timmy was playing in the backyard. His dad had just given him a brand new toy jeep. It was a special red jeep and it was very fragile.
Timmy was going to show his friend, Sarah, the jeep. Suddenly, the neighbor's cat came into the yard. Sarah gasped, "Oh no! The cat is going to eat the jeep!"
Timmy quickly ran over to the jeep and picked it up. He started to run around the yard, looking for a place to hide the jeep from the cat. He spotted some bushes and ran over. He quickly put the jeep in the bushes and covered it with some leaves.
The cat was still chasing Timmy, but he managed to stay one step ahead of it. Finally, he spotted a tree and quickly climbed up. After a few seconds, the cat stopped and gave up.
When Timmy got down from the tree, he was relieved to find that the jeep was still safe. Sarah and Timmy ran to the bushes, gleefully uncovering the jeep. Sarah smiled and said, "Wow, that was a close call!"
The two friends quickly started playing with the jeep and continued enjoying their day in the backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a lively bear who loved to watch. He watched the birds fly in the sky, he watched the sun move across the horizon and he watched the fish swim in the river.
One day, the bear watched as a fisherman walked by with a long spear. The bear asked the fisherman what he would do with his spear and the fisherman said that he was going to catch some fish. The lively bear was so excited to watch that he started to jump and dance around in circles.
The fisherman laughed and said "I can see that you like watching. You can come with me and you can help me catch those fish." So, the bear and the fisherman went fishing.
Soon, the river was teeming with fish, but the lively bear noticed that most of them were too fast for the fisherman's spear. One little fish, much slower than the rest, swam past and the bear pointed to it. The bear said, "I think you should watch for that one, it's not as fast as the others."
So the fisherman watched, and sure enough the slow fish swam right into the end of his spear! The bear cheered and the fisherman thanked the bear for his help catching the fish. From then on, they went fishing together, the lively bear helping the fisherman watch for fish.

Suddenly, the bird stood up, its feathers ruffled. It said to the girl, "I was flying over the river and the sky suddenly went dark! A loud noise came and knocked me down, now I'm dead. 
The girl was shocked. "But why did it happen?" she asked. 
The bird replied, "Many years ago, people did something bad and now the sky is punishing us!" 
The girl thought for a moment, then stood up to leave quietly. She knew that she must protect the environment so dangerous things like this would not happen.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy bear. One day he was walking in the forest, when he noticed something strange. It was a leak coming from the river. He decided to explore, and as he got closer he heard a sound. 
It was a sharp sound like a rock was being cut. He squinted, but he couldn't see where it was coming from. Suddenly he saw a glint in the water. He realised it was a sharp knife!
He didn't know what to do, so he shouted out.
"What are you doing?"
The knife stopped and a little fox peeped out.
"I'm trying to fix this leak," she said. 
The clumsy bear was amazed. He thought for a moment and then he said, "Let me help you. I'm clumsy, but with both of us here I'm sure we can fix it." 
The fox smiled, and together they worked until the leak was fixed. The bear was very proud of his work, and the fox was much happier.
And that is the story of the clumsy bear and the leak.

Once upon a time, there was a pigeon who wanted to fly. He hopped around, looking for a way to take to th sky.

"That's the place for you, Mr. Pigeon!" said the boy.

When Jake finally arrived, he was so excited. He saw pretty sand and lots of cheap things he could buy. He was running around and looking at everything when he heard a voice. A man had a table that was full of things for sale. He said, "Welcome to the beach, young man. What can I do for you?"
Jake smiled and said, "I'd like to buy some of those cheap things you have there." The man laughed and said, "You must have a good eye for a bargain! Go ahead, take a look around."
Jake had a great time looking at all the different items. He felt like he had made a great discovery and was happy with his purchase. When he got home, he knew he had made the right choice. He wondered what else he would find the next time he went to the beach.

One day, the rain finally stopped, but it was too late. The monkey had gotten very sick and couldn't move anymore. It died in its tree, all alone. The other animals in the forest were very sad and missed their cheerful monkey friend.

Timmy nodded and said, "Yes, I did. But it was yucky. I don't like bitter things."
Lily laughed and said, "You can't eat bushes! Let's go write our names in the sand instead." And they both ran off to play in the sand.

Lily took her tired self and her pencil and sat down to draw with her brother. They drew pictures of animals, flowers, and even a big house. It was a lot of fun and Lily didn't feel tired anymore. She realized that spending time with her brother was more important than just drawing by herself.

The next day, Lily went to Jack's house and they played together again. They had a lovely time and became good friends. From then on, they would meet at the park every day to play together. And Lily knew that if she ever lost Jack again, she could count on her mom's network to help her find him.

"It looks fair," said Jill.

"I think they look so tasty," said Jack.
Jill nodded her head. "I agree, they are very nice," she said.

"We're too lazy," they said.
The little rabbit thought for a minute. Then he had an idea.
"Let's get some fruit," he said. "We can get some apples, oranges and bananas. That will be fun!"
So the group of animals all got up and went out to get some fruit. They had a great time picking the fruit, and when they were finished, they all felt much better.
The next day, the group of animals had so much energy that none of them wanted to sleep. They decided to go for a walk instead, and have lots of fun together.
The group of animals learned a valuable lesson that day - that being lazy is not always the best choice. Sometimes getting up and doing something can be much more fun!

"Oh no, now I'm all messy!" Pat said, looking sad.
She looked around for something to help her clean up, when she noticed something in the corner. It was a big box of cleaning supplies. Pat found a towel and started to clean up carefully. Once she was spotless, Pat smiled and thanked the hallway for being so careless. 
Pat thought it was the best find ever and went back to the living room to tell her mom all her adventures.

"I am trying to get some vegetables," the farmer said.

The farmer followed the rabbit through the woods. Finally they found a beautiful garden filled with all sorts of vegetables. The farmer was so excited!
He thanked the rabbit, and the two of them began to pick the vegetables. Soon enough, the farmer had gained all the vegetables he needed. He thanked the rabbit once again, waved goodbye, and headed home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lilly. Lilly loved counting. Everywhere she went she would count to make sure everything was in order. 
One day, Lilly went into the garden and saw a pistol. She was excited but scared at the same time. Lilly's dad had always told her to never touch it. 
"What should I do with it?" She thought. 
Then Lilly had an idea. She decided to count the pistol. She started counting the barrel, the handle, the bullets, and all the pieces of the pistol until she reached 10. 
Lilly backed away slowly. Suddenly, her dad walked into the garden. 
"What are you doing?" He said.
Lilly answered timidly, "I was counting the pistol because it looked so spicy that I wanted to make sure it was safe!"
Her dad smiled. He was pleased with her clever solution and said, "Well done Lilly! Counting is a very important skill." 
The moral of Lilly's story is that counting helps us stay safe and it can be fun too!

Suddenly, a frog jumped up from the pond! "I waited until the weeds died," it said. "Now I can swim!"
The duck was so surprised that he splashed in the water too! The frog and the duck had a lot of fun swimming together.
They swam for hours and hours until the sun went down. Finally, the duck said goodbye and flew away, but the frog stayed near his pond, ready to splash again the next day.

"Lucy, you mustn't pick the flower," said her mom.
"Why not?" asked Lucy.
"It's a delicate flower and picking it would prevent it from growing," explained her mom.
Lucy understood, so she squatted next to the flower and admired it instead. She thanked her mom for helping her make the right decision. Then they both happily walked home together.

The bird replied, "I'm just so happy! I've been waiting for someone as fast as you to come my way. Now we can race around the pond together and see who is the fastest!"
The duck was excited. He loved race, especially if it meant he could show off his speed.
So the yellow duck and noisy bird raced around the pond together. They flew fast and they flew furious. It was a close race, but in the end, the duck won. He was proud of his win and so was the bird. From then on, they were the best of friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Timmy. Timmy lived on the shore with his family. Timmy was a modest crab, and he liked to stay hidden in his little cave. One day, Timmy was walking along the shore when he saw a big seagull. The seagull was looking at Timmy with hungry eyes.
Timmy knew he had to be careful. He scurried away as fast as he could. But the seagull was too fast. Just as the seagull was about to snap his beak shut on Timmy, Timmy had an idea. He quickly ran to his little cave and hid inside. The seagull couldn't get to him in there.
From that day on, Timmy never ventured too far from his little cave. He knew that the seagull might be watching, and he didn't want to get snapped up. Timmy was happy to be safe and sound in his modest little home.

"What is that?" Tom asked. He looked closer and saw a small, furry animal. It had big ears, a long tail, and black and white stripes. It looked at them with bright eyes.
"I don't know," Lily said. "It is an unknown animal. Maybe it is a cat, but a different kind of cat."
The animal made a noise. It sounded like a hiss. It showed its teeth. It did not look happy.
"Uh-oh," Tom said. "I think it is angry. Maybe we should put the rock back."
They quickly moved the stick and let the rock fall back. The animal disappeared under the rock. They heard another hiss.
"Let's go," Lily said. "We don't want to make it more angry. Maybe we can find another rock with a nicer animal."
They ran away from the rock and looked for another place to play. They did not know that they had found a skunk, and that they were lucky that it did not spray them.

Ben does not like to lose. He grabs one of Lily's red soldiers and hides it under his pillow. "Now we have the same!" he says. "Three and three!"
Lily sees what Ben did. She is angry. She grabs two of Ben's blue soldiers and throws them in the trash. "Now I have more again!" she says. "Three and zero!"
Ben sees what Lily did. He is sad. He starts to cry. "That's not fair!" he says. "You cheated!"
Lily feels sorry for Ben. She knows she was wrong. She takes the blue soldiers out of the trash and the red soldier out of the pillow. She gives them back to Ben. "I'm sorry, Ben," she says. "You can have your soldiers. Let's play nice."
Ben stops crying. He smiles at Lily. He hugs her. "Thank you, Lily," he says. "You are a good friend. Let's play nice."
Lily and Ben hug each other. They decide to make their soldiers march together. They are quiet and happy. They are good friends.

"OK, but you have to be careful. It is very fast and loud. And you have to promise to clean it after we are done," Anna said.
"I promise, I promise," Ben said. He took the mixer and plugged it in. He put some eggs and flour and sugar in the bowl. He turned on the mixer and held it over the bowl.
But the mixer was too fast and loud for Ben. He got scared and let go of the mixer. The mixer flew out of his hand and splattered eggs and flour and sugar all over the kitchen. The mixer landed on the floor and made a big noise.
Anna and Ben were shocked. The kitchen was filthy. There was mess everywhere. They heard Mom coming.
"Oh no, Mom will be so mad. What do we do?" Anna said.
"I don't know. I'm sorry, Anna. I broke my promise. I didn't clean the mixer. I made a big mess," Ben said.
They heard Mom open the door. They looked at her with big eyes. They hoped she would not be too angry.

Here is one possible story, but there are many other ways to write it.
Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big dog near the fence. The dog was barking and jumping. Lily and Ben were scared of the dog.
"Let's move away from the dog," Lily said. "He might bite us."
"OK," Ben said. "But how do we move? The dog is blocking the gate."
Lily looked around. She saw a person sitting on a bench. The person had a book and a hat. Lily had an idea.
"Let's ask the person for help," Lily said. "Maybe the person knows the dog."
"OK," Ben said. "But be careful. The person might be mean."
Lily and Ben walked slowly to the bench. They said hello to the person. The person smiled and said hello back.
"Can you help us?" Lily asked. "We are scared of the dog. He is barking and jumping. We want to move away from him."
The person looked at the dog. The person said, "Don't be scared. The dog is not mean. He is just excited. He is my dog. His name is Max. He likes to play. Do you want to play with him?"
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They were not sure. The dog was big and loud.
"Can we pet him?" Ben asked.
"Sure," the person said. "He likes to be petted. He is very soft and friendly. Come, I will show you."
The person got up and walked to the fence. The person called Max and told him to sit. Max stopped barking and jumping. He sat and wagged his tail. The person petted Max and gave him a treat.
"See? He is a good dog," the person said. "Do you want to try?"
Lily and Ben nodded. They moved closer to the fence. They reached out their hands and touched Max. Max licked their hands and nuzzled their faces. Lily and Ben giggled. They were not scared anymore. They liked Max.
"Thank you for helping us," Lily said to the person.
"You're welcome," the person said. "I'm glad you like Max. He likes you too. Do you want to play with him some more?"
"Yes, please," Ben said.
Lily and Ben played with Max and the person. They had fun. They forgot about the slide, the swing and the run. They made a new friend.

"Are you ready?" their mom asked. "The driver is here to take us to the airport."
"Yes, mom!" Lily and Tom said. They ran to the door with their bags. They saw a big car with a driver. The driver smiled and helped them put their bags in the trunk.
"Hello, I'm Sam. I'm your driver today," he said. "Are you excited to see your grandma?"
"Yes, we are!" Lily and Tom said. They got in the car and buckled their seatbelts. Sam started the car and drove away.
On the way to the airport, they saw many things. They saw trees and houses and shops and people. They also saw another car that had an accident. The car was broken and the people looked hurt.
"Oh no, what happened?" Lily asked.
"There was a crash," Sam said. "Sometimes cars hit each other and make a loud noise. Then the cars and the people get hurt. That's why we have to be careful and follow the rules when we drive."
"Will they be okay?" Tom asked.
"I hope so," Sam said. "There are helpers who come to help them. They are called police and ambulance. They check if the people are hurt and take them to the hospital. They also fix the cars or take them away."
Lily and Tom felt sad for the people who were hurt. They hoped they would get better soon. They also felt happy that Sam was a good driver and kept them safe. They thanked him and gave him a hug when they got to the airport. They were ready to fly to their grandma.

Tom and Sam are very sorry. They realize they made a big mistake. They were very selfish and noisy. They did not respect their moms or the other people. They missed a chance to watch a nice movie and have fun.
They say sorry to their moms. They promise to be good and quiet next time. They learn their lesson. They understand that sometimes they have to listen to their moms and be polite and patient. They hug their moms and say they love them. Their moms forgive them and hug them back. They love them too.

We will need some wood and some nails and some hammer and some paint. It will be fun and easy. And when we are done, we will have a new and strong and beautiful fence. And you will have your ball back. Are you ready?"
Lily and Tom said, "Yes, Mr. Lee. We are ready. Let's repair the fence!"
They followed Mr. Lee to his yard. They worked together to repair the fence. They learned how to measure and cut and nail and paint. They had fun and they made a new friend. They repaired the fence and they got their ball back. They thanked Mr. Lee and they hugged him. They said, "Thank you, Mr. Lee. You are very kind and friendly. You helped us repair the fence and you gave us our ball back. We like you and we like our new fence. We will not kick the ball too hard again. We will be good neighbors."
Mr. Lee said, "You are very welcome, Lily and Tom. You are very kind and friendly too. You helped me repair the fence and you said you were sorry. I like you and I like our new fence too. We will be good neighbors. And you can play with your ball anytime. Just be careful and have fun."
Lily and Tom said, "Thank you, Mr. Lee. We will be careful and have fun. Goodbye, Mr. Lee."
They waved goodbye to Mr. Lee and they ran back to their yard. They played with their ball and they admired their new fence. They were happy and proud. They learned how to repair the fence and how to be good neighbors.
The moral of the story is: If you break something, you should say you are sorry and help to fix it. If you help someone, you can make a new friend. If you are careful and respectful, you can have fun and be happy.

He looks at Sara's tower. He thinks, "Sara is so creative. She can make anything. I can't make anything. I want her tower. Maybe if I take her tower, I can make one too."
He waits until Sara is not looking. He sneaks to her tower and grabs the handle. He tries to pull it, but it is too heavy. He pulls harder and harder, but it does not move. He does not know that Sara used glue to support her tower and make it strong.
Sara hears a loud noise. She turns around and sees Tom pulling her tower. She sees her tower breaking and falling apart. She sees her blocks scattering on the floor. She sees Tom holding the handle and looking surprised.
She is very angry and sad. She shouts, "Tom, what did you do? You broke my tower! You ruined my blocks! You are a bad friend!"
Tom feels sorry and scared. He drops the handle and says, "I'm sorry, Sara. I just wanted to make a tower like yours. I didn't mean to break it."
But Sara does not listen. She runs to the teacher and tells her what Tom did. The teacher comes and scolds Tom. She makes him pick up the blocks and put them back in the box. She makes him sit in the corner and think about what he did.
Sara does not play with Tom anymore. She plays with other friends who are creative and nice. Tom is alone and sad. He wishes he did not break Sara's tower. He wishes he was a better friend.

It was a cold night and Tom and Lily were getting ready for bed. They put on their warm pajamas and brushed their teeth. They said good night to their mom and dad and went to their room.
"Can we read a story, please?" Lily asked Tom. She loved stories, especially about animals and fairies.
"Okay, but only one," Tom said. He was older than Lily and liked to act like a big brother. He picked a book from the shelf and opened it on the bed. "This one is about a mouse who lives in a chimney."
"A chimney? What is that?" Lily asked.
Tom pointed to the picture in the book. "It's a big pipe on the roof where the smoke comes out when you make a fire. The mouse likes to live there because it's warm and cozy."
They started to read the story. The mouse had many adventures in the chimney, but he also had to be careful of the cat and the owl who wanted to catch him. He made friends with a sparrow and a squirrel who helped him find food and escape danger.
Lily listened with wide eyes and asked many questions. Tom tried to answer them, but he also wanted to finish the story. He liked the mouse, too, and wanted to know how it ended.
They read until they reached the last page. The mouse had found a new home in a barn, where he was safe and happy. He still visited the chimney sometimes, but only when he was sure there was no fire.
The end, Tom said and closed the book.
"Did you like the story, Lily?" he asked.
"Yes, I did. The mouse was very brave and smart. And he had nice friends. Can we read another one?" Lily said.
"No, Lily, it's time to sleep now. We have to be quiet and settle down. Mom and dad will be angry if we stay up too late," Tom said.
He turned off the light and tucked Lily in her bed. He gave her a kiss on the cheek and said, "Good night, Lily. Sweet dreams."
"Good night, Tom. Thank you for the story," Lily said.
They closed their eyes and fell asleep, dreaming of the mouse and the chimney.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their dog, Max. They liked to run and jump and slide and swing. They had a lot of fun.
But then the sky became gray and the air became cold. A thick fog came and covered everything. Ben and Lily could not see the trees or the flowers or the birds. They could only see each other and Max.
"Where is Mommy?" Lily asked. She was scared and hungry.
"I don't know," Ben said. He was scared and hungry too. "Maybe she is looking for us. We have to remain here and wait for her. She will find us soon."
They hugged each other and Max. They hoped Mommy would come soon.
Mommy was in the car. She had gone to buy some snacks for Ben and Lily. She was on her way back to the park when the fog came. She could not see the road or the signs or the lights. She was worried and confused.
She tried to call Ben and Lily on her phone, but there was no signal. She tried to find the park, but she got lost. She hoped Ben and Lily were safe and warm.
She drove slowly and carefully. She looked for any sign of the park. She prayed for the fog to go away.
After a long time, she saw a faint shape in the fog. It was a slide. She had found the park. She parked the car and ran to the slide. She saw three more shapes in the fog. They were Ben and Lily and Max.
"Mommy!" Ben and Lily shouted. They ran to her and hugged her. Max barked and wagged his tail.
"Ben! Lily! Max! I'm so glad to see you!" Mommy said. She hugged them back. She was happy and relieved.
"I'm sorry I took so long. The fog was very bad. I got lost. Are you okay?" Mommy asked.
"We're okay, Mommy. We were scared and hungry, but we remained here and waited for you. We knew you would find us," Ben said.
"You were very brave and smart, Ben. And you too, Lily. And you too, Max. I'm very proud of you," Mommy said.
She gave them the snacks she had bought. They ate them and felt better. The fog started to clear. They could see the sun and the sky and the colors again.
They got in the car and drove home. They were happy and safe. They remained together.

Lila and Tom were twins who loved to explore. They had a big spaceship that could take them to different planets. One day, they decided to visit a planet that was green and blue, with many animals and plants.
"Look, Lila, a bird!" Tom said, pointing to a colorful creature that flew in the sky. "It is so pretty!"
"Let's go and say hello to it!" Lila said, jumping out of the spaceship. She ran after the bird, trying to catch it.
"Wait, Lila, be careful!" Tom said, following her. "We don't know if the bird is friendly or not. And we have to behave on this planet. We are guests here."
But Lila did not listen. She chased the bird until it landed on a branch. She reached out her hand to touch it, but the bird did not like that. It pecked her finger and made a loud noise.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Lila cried, pulling back her hand. "That hurt!"
The noise scared the other animals, who came out of their hiding places. They saw the twins and did not like them either. They started to growl and snarl, showing their teeth and claws.
"Uh-oh, Lila, we are in trouble!" Tom said, grabbing her hand. "We have to go back to the spaceship, now!"
They ran as fast as they could, dodging the angry animals. They reached the spaceship and jumped inside. They closed the door and flew away.
"Wow, that was scary!" Lila said, rubbing her finger. "I'm sorry, Tom. I should have listened to you. I did not behave on this planet."
"It's okay, Lila. I'm glad you are safe." Tom said, hugging her. "But maybe next time, we should find a more charming planet to visit. One where the animals are nice and friendly."

"Dead," she read.
Lily and Tom looked at each other. They did not know what that word meant. They thought it was a funny sound.

Tim and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big vine that grew on the wall. It had many green leaves and purple flowers.
"Let's climb the vine!" Tim said. "It looks like fun!"
Lily was not sure. "But what if we fall? Or what if Mom and Dad get angry?"
Tim shrugged. "Don't be scared. They won't see us. And the vine is tough. It can hold us."
He grabbed the vine and started to pull himself up. Lily followed him, but she felt nervous. The vine was high and wobbly.
They reached the top of the wall and looked around. They saw the neighbor's dog, a big and black one. It barked at them and ran towards the wall.
"Uh-oh!" Tim said. "The dog is mad at us! We have to go down!"
They tried to slide down the vine, but it was not easy. The vine was rough and scratchy. It hurt their hands and legs. The dog jumped and snapped at them.
"Help!" Lily cried. "Mom! Dad!"
Mom and Dad heard them and came outside. They saw Tim and Lily on the vine and the dog on the ground. They were shocked and worried.
"Tim! Lily! What are you doing?" Mom shouted. "Get down from there!"
Dad grabbed a stick and scared the dog away. He helped Tim and Lily down from the vine. They were dirty and bleeding.
Mom hugged them and checked their wounds. She was angry and sad.
"Why did you climb the vine?" she asked. "You could have been hurt badly! Or bitten by the dog! You know you are not allowed to do that!"
Tim and Lily looked down. They felt sorry and ashamed.
"We wanted to have fun," Tim said. "We thought the vine was tough."
"But it was not safe," Lily said. "We were wrong."
Mom and Dad took them inside and cleaned their wounds. They gave them a hug and a kiss.
"We love you, Tim and Lily," they said. "But you have to be careful and listen to us. We only want you to be safe and happy."
Tim and Lily nodded. They learned their lesson. They never climbed the vine again.

Tim and Sam love to play hockey. They have sticks and a ball and a net in the yard. They play every day after school. They are good friends and have fun.
One day, it is very cold outside. The wind blows hard and the snow falls. Tim and Sam put on their coats and hats and gloves and boots. They want to play hockey. They go to the yard and start to play.
But soon, they feel very cold. They shiver and their noses turn red. They can't hold their sticks well. They miss the ball and the net. They are not having fun.
They see a boy walking by. He has no coat or hat or gloves or boots. He has only a thin shirt and pants and shoes. He shivers more than Tim and Sam. He looks very sad. He is poor.
Tim and Sam stop playing. They feel sorry for the boy. They call him over. They say, "Hi, we are Tim and Sam. Do you want to play hockey with us? You can use our coat and hat and gloves and boots. We can share."
The boy smiles. He says, "Thank you, Tim and Sam. You are very kind. I would love to play hockey with you. My name is Ben."
Tim and Sam give Ben their coat and hat and gloves and boots. They play hockey together. They take turns using the sticks and the ball and the net. They have fun.
They are not cold anymore. They are warm. They are warm in their bodies and in their hearts. They are friends.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring.

One night, they heard a loud noise. It was a bear! The bear was hungry and smelled their food. It came near the tent and tried to open it. Anna and Ben were scared. They hugged each other and whispered.
"Mom, dad, help!" Anna said.
"Shh, don't make noise. Maybe it will go away." Ben said.
But the bear did not go away. It ripped the tent with its claws and poked its head inside. It saw Anna and Ben and growled. They felt helpless. They could not run or hide.
Then they heard another noise. It was their dad! He had a flashlight and a stick. He waved the flashlight at the bear and shouted.
"Go away, bear! Leave us alone!"
The bear was surprised and scared. It did not like the bright light and the loud voice. It backed away and ran into the woods. Anna and Ben's dad came inside the tent and hugged them.
"Are you okay, kids? Don't worry, the bear is gone. You are safe." He said.
"Thank you, dad. You are brave." Anna said.
"Yes, thank you, dad. You saved us." Ben said.
They smiled and cuddled with their mom and dad. They were happy and relieved. They did not want to see the bear again. They hoped it would find some other food. They fell asleep in their tent and dreamed of nice things.

"OK, Sam, that sounds fun!" Tom says. He follows Sam to the pond. They sit on the grass and throw the hook into the water. They wait for a fish to bite.
But no fish comes. They wait and wait and wait. They feel bored and hungry.
"Maybe the fish do not like our hook," Tom says. "Maybe we need some bait."
"Bait? What is bait?" Sam asks.
"Bait is something that the fish like to eat," Tom says. "Like worms or bread or cheese."
"Where can we find some bait?" Sam asks.
Tom looks around. He sees a big trash can near the pond. He smells something smelly.
"Maybe there is some bait in there," Tom says. He gets up and walks to the trash can. He opens the lid and looks inside.
"Yuck!" Tom says. He sees many rotten things in the trash can. He feels sick.
"What did you find, Tom?" Sam asks.
"Nothing good, Sam," Tom says. "Only smelly trash. Let's go home. I do not want to catch fish anymore."
"Me neither, Tom," Sam says. "Let's go home and have some cookies."
They leave the rod and the hook on the grass. They run to their homes. They forget about the fish and the pond. They only want cookies.

Ben and Lily were playing by the river. They liked to throw stones and watch the water splash. Sometimes they saw fish or frogs or ducks. But they never saw a crocodile.
One day, they found a big rope near the river. Ben had an idea. He said, "Let's tie the rope to a tree and swing over the water. It will be fun!" Lily nodded. She liked to swing.
They tied the rope to a strong tree and took turns to swing. They laughed and shouted as they flew over the river. They did not see the eyes and teeth under the water. They did not hear the growl.
The crocodile was hungry. It saw the children swinging over the water. It waited for the right moment. It jumped out of the water and snapped its jaws at Ben's feet. Ben screamed. He let go of the rope and fell into the water. The crocodile grabbed his leg and pulled him under.
Lily saw what happened. She was scared. She ran to the tree and grabbed the rope. She swung over the water and shouted, "Ben, Ben, where are you?" She hoped he was okay.
She saw Ben's head pop out of the water. He was bleeding and crying. He said, "Help, help, the crocodile has me!" He tried to kick the crocodile, but it was too strong. He felt helpless.
Lily was brave. She swung closer to Ben and reached out her hand. She said, "Ben, grab my hand, I'll pull you out!" Ben saw her hand and grabbed it. Lily pulled with all her might. The crocodile let go of Ben's leg and snapped at Lily's hand. But it was too late. Lily and Ben swung back to the shore. They were safe.
They hugged each other and cried. They were happy to be alive. They ran away from the river and never played there again. They learned to be careful of crocodiles.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the bakery with her mom. She saw many yummy pastries in the window. She wanted to try them all. She was very curious about how they tasted.
"Mom, can I have a pastry, please?" she asked.
"Sure, honey, you can choose one. But only one, okay?" her mom said.
Lily looked at all the pastries. She saw a big croissant, a round donut, a square brownie, and a star-shaped cookie. She decided to pick the cookie. It had colorful sprinkles on it.
"Here you go, Lily. Enjoy your cookie," the baker said, handing her the pastry.
"Thank you, Mr. Baker," Lily said, smiling.
Lily and her mom walked out of the bakery. Lily took a bite of her cookie. It was sweet and crunchy. She liked it very much. But then she saw a boy eating a croissant. It looked flaky and buttery. She wondered how it tasted.
"Mom, can I have a croissant, too?" she asked.
"No, Lily, you already have a cookie. You can't have two pastries. That's too much sugar," her mom said.
"But I want to try the croissant. It looks so good," Lily said.
She had an idea. She saw a trash can nearby. She thought she could replace her cookie with a croissant. She threw her cookie in the trash can when her mom was not looking. Then she ran back to the bakery.
"Mr. Baker, can I have a croissant, please?" she asked.
"Didn't you just get a cookie, Lily?" the baker asked.
"I lost it. It fell on the ground," Lily lied.
The baker frowned. He did not believe her. He saw her throw her cookie in the trash can. He knew she was not telling the truth.
"I'm sorry, Lily, but I can't give you a croissant. You should be happy with what you have. And you should not lie. Lying is bad. It makes people sad and angry. You should say sorry to your mom and to me," the baker said.
Lily felt ashamed. She realized she made a mistake. She wasted her cookie and she lied to the baker and to her mom. She did not get to try the croissant. And she lost her cookie. She was very sorry.

"That's okay, Lily. I'm happy that you said sorry. Saying sorry is good. It shows that you care and that you want to do better. Next time, be happy with what you have. And don't lie. Lying is bad. It hurts people and yourself. Do you understand?" the baker said.
"Yes, Mr. Baker. I understand. Thank you for forgiving me," Lily said.

"Mom, I'm sorry. I lied to you. I threw my cookie in the trash can. I wanted to try the croissant. But I was wrong. I should have been happy with my cookie. It was very yummy. And I should not have lied to you and to Mr. Baker. I'm very sorry," Lily said.

"Her name is Lily, and this is Pinky," her mom said. "She likes dolls. Do you want to play with her?"
The boy nodded. He put his car on the ground and sat next to Lily. He reached out his hand to touch Pinky.
"Can I see your doll?" he asked.
Lily shrugged. She did not mind if he saw Pinky, but she did not want him to take her away. She held Pinky close to her chest.
"She's very pretty," the boy said. "I like her pink dress. Can I hold her for a minute?"
Lily looked at her mom. Her mom smiled and nodded. Lily hesitated, but then she decided to be brave. She handed Pinky to the boy.
"Thank you," the boy said. He held Pinky gently and smiled. "She's very soft. Do you want to see my car?"
Lily nodded. She was curious about his car. He gave her his car and showed her how to make it go.
"Vroom, vroom!" he said. "It's very fast. Do you like cars?"
Lily shrugged. She did not like cars as much as dolls, but she liked playing with the boy. He was nice and funny. She smiled and said, "Yes, I like cars."
They played together for a while, until their moms called them to go home. They exchanged their toys and said goodbye.
"Bye, Lily. Bye, Pinky. See you again," the boy said.
"Bye, bye. See you again," Lily said.
She hugged Pinky and waved to the boy. She was not shy anymore. She had made a new friend.

Sara and Ben were playing in the backyard. They found a big box and some old nails. They wanted to make a house for their toys.
"Look, I have a hammer!" Ben said. He picked up a heavy tool and hit a nail into the box. "Bang, bang, bang!"
"Be careful, Ben!" Sara said. "You might hurt yourself. Let me help you." She took another nail and tried to hammer it in. But the nail was too hard and the box was too soft. The nail bent and fell out.
"Oh no!" Sara said. "This nail is bad. We need a new one."
"No, we don't," Ben said. "We just need to believe. If we believe hard enough, the nail will work. Watch me!" He picked up the bent nail and held it in his hand. He closed his eyes and said, "I believe, I believe, I believe!"
Then he opened his eyes and smiled. He showed Sara the nail. It was straight and shiny.
"Wow!" Sara said. "How did you do that?"
"I told you, I believed," Ben said. "Now you try. Believe and you can do anything."
Sara nodded. She took the nail and held it in her hand. She closed her eyes and said, "I believe, I believe, I believe!"
She opened her eyes and looked at the nail. It was still bent and dull.
"It didn't work," Sara said. "Why not?"
"Maybe you didn't believe hard enough," Ben said. "Or maybe you need a different nail. Here, take this one. It's bigger and stronger."
Sara took the new nail and tried again. She closed her eyes and said, "I believe, I believe, I believe!"
She opened her eyes and looked at the nail. It was still big and strong.
"It worked!" Sara said. "Thank you, Ben!"
"You're welcome, Sara," Ben said. "Now let's finish our house. We can do it if we believe."

"Let's have some cake," Tom said. "Mom won't notice."
"No, Tom, we can't," Lily said. "That cake is for Dad. Mom said we have to wait until he comes home."
But Tom did not listen. He climbed on a chair and reached for the cake. He took a big bite and smiled.
"Mmm, this is delicious," he said. "Come on, Lily, have some too."
Lily shook her head. She knew it was wrong to take the cake. She got off the chair and ran to the living room. She wanted to be quiet and not get in trouble.
Soon, Mom came into the kitchen. She saw the cake with a big bite missing. She was very angry.
"Who did this?" she asked. "Who took a bite of Dad's cake?"
Tom hid behind the chair. He was scared. He knew he had done a bad thing.
Lily came back to the kitchen. She saw Mom and Tom. She felt sorry for Tom, but she also wanted to tell the truth.
"It was Tom, Mom," she said. "He reached for the cake and ate some. I told him not to, but he did not listen."
Mom looked at Tom. He came out from behind the chair. He hung his head and said sorry.
Mom was still angry, but she was also glad that Lily was honest. She hugged Lily and said, "Thank you, Lily, for telling the truth. That was very brave and good of you. You can have a small piece of cake later, after Dad comes home."
She looked at Tom and said, "Tom, you were very naughty and greedy. You spoiled Dad's cake and you lied to me. You can't have any cake today. You have to go to your room and think about what you did."
Tom felt very sad and ashamed. He wished he had listened to Lily. He learned his lesson. He said sorry to Mom and Dad and Lily. He promised to be good and share next time.
