Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they found a stream near their house. The stream had clear water and many stones and fish. Tom and Lily wanted to play in the stream.
"Let's make a bridge with the stones," Tom said. "We can cross the stream and see what is on the other side."
"OK," Lily said. "But be careful not to fall in the water. It is cold and deep."
They started to pile up the stones in the middle of the stream. They worked hard and had fun. They made a bridge that was big enough for them to walk on.
"Look, we did it!" Tom said. "Let's go over the bridge and explore."
They walked on the bridge, holding hands. But when they reached the middle, they saw something that made them scared. It was an enormous frog that was sitting on the last stone. The frog had big eyes and a wide mouth. It croaked loudly and jumped towards them.
"Ribbit! Ribbit! This is my bridge. Go away!" the frog said.
Tom and Lily screamed and ran back to the shore. They dropped their hands and fell on the grass. They were wet and dirty and frightened.
"Are you OK?" Tom asked Lily.
"Yes, I'm OK," Lily said. "But that was a mean frog. He scared us and ruined our bridge."
They looked at the stream and saw the frog sitting on the bridge again. He was smiling and croaking.
"Ribbit! Ribbit! This is my bridge. I like it. Thank you for making it for me," the frog said.
Tom and Lily felt angry and sad. They had worked hard to make the bridge, and they wanted to play on it. But the frog took it from them and did not share.
"That is not fair," Tom said. "He should share the bridge with us. We made it together."
"Yes, he should," Lily said. "But he is bigger and stronger than us. We can't make him move."
They thought for a while. Then they had an idea.
"Maybe we can make another bridge," Tom said. "But this time, we can make it with sticks and leaves. The frog won't like it. He will leave it alone."
"Good idea," Lily said. "Let's try it."
They gathered some sticks and leaves from the ground. They made another bridge with them, next to the stone bridge. The bridge was not as strong or as pretty as the stone bridge, but it was enough for them to cross the stream.
They walked on the new bridge, holding hands again. They reached the other side and saw a meadow with flowers and butterflies. They smiled and played in the meadow. They forgot about the frog and the stone bridge.
The frog saw them and felt curious. He wondered what was on the other side of the stream. He decided to try the new bridge. He jumped on it, but it was not solid or stable. It broke under his weight and he fell in the water. He splashed and struggled and cried for help.
"Help! Help! I can't swim!" the frog said.
Tom and Lily heard him and looked back. They saw the frog in the water, and the broken bridge. They felt sorry for him. They remembered that he was a living thing, and that he needed help.
"Let's help him," Tom said. "He is in trouble. Maybe he will be nice to us if we help him."
"OK," Lily said. "But how can we help him?"
They looked around and saw a big leaf floating on the water. They ran to the leaf and pushed it towards the frog. The frog saw the leaf and grabbed it. He climbed on it and floated to the shore. He was wet and cold and ashamed.
"Thank you for helping me," the frog said. "I'm sorry for being mean to you. I was selfish and greedy. I should have shared the bridge with you. Can you forgive me?"
Tom and Lily looked at each other and nodded. They forgave the frog. They felt happy and proud. They had learned a lesson.
"Sharing is caring," Tom said. "We can all play together and have fun."
"Yes, sharing is caring," Lily said. "We can be friends and help each other."
They invited the frog to join them in the meadow. The frog accepted and smiled. He learned a lesson too.
They played in the meadow, with the flowers and the butterflies. They crossed the stream, with the stone bridge and the leaf. They were happy and peaceful. They were friends.

Sara and Ben are friends who live next to each other. Sara has a big tree in her yard. She likes to climb the tree and swing from the branches. Ben does not have a tree in his yard. He only has a small bush. He is envious of Sara's tree. He wishes he could own the tree.
One day, Ben decides to sneak into Sara's yard and cut the tree. He thinks that if he cuts the tree, Sara will not have it anymore and he will not be envious. He takes a saw and starts to cut the tree. But the tree is very strong and does not fall. Instead, the saw gets stuck in the tree and Ben cannot pull it out. He hears Sara coming and runs away.
Sara sees the saw in her tree and is very sad. She wonders who did this to her tree. She asks her mom and dad, but they do not know. She asks Ben, but he lies and says he does not know. Sara feels hurt and angry. She does not want to be friends with Ben anymore.
The next day, a big storm comes. The wind blows hard and the rain pours down. Sara's tree is still standing, but Ben's bush is blown away. Ben has nothing in his yard. He feels sorry for what he did to Sara's tree. He realizes that he was wrong to be envious and to hurt Sara's tree. He decides to tell Sara the truth and to say sorry.
He goes to Sara's yard and knocks on her door. Sara opens the door and sees Ben. She is surprised and still mad. Ben tells her that he was the one who cut her tree. He says that he was envious of her tree and that he wanted to own it. He says that he is very sorry and that he will never do it again. He asks Sara to forgive him and to be friends again.
Sara listens to Ben and sees that he is sincere. She remembers that Ben is her friend and that he made a mistake. She decides to forgive him and to be friends again. She tells him that he does not need to own a tree to be happy. She says that they can share her tree and play together. Ben is happy and grateful. He thanks Sara and hugs her. They go to the tree and swing from the branches. They are both happy.
The moral of the story is: Do not be envious of what others have. Be content with what you have. Do not hurt others or their things. Be honest and apologize when you do something wrong. Forgive and be friends. Share and be happy.

"Not now, Anna. It is still daytime. We have to wait until it is dark. Then we can count the stars together." her mom says.
"Okay, mom. I will wait. But can I count something else until then?" Anna says.
"Sure, Anna. You can count anything you want. Just remember to ask me first." her mom says.
"Okay, mom. Thank you. I love you." Anna says.
"I love you too, Anna. You are my smart and sweet girl." her mom says.

Tom and Sue are friends who live on a farm. They like to help their parents with the animals and the plants. One day, they have a special job. They have to deliver eggs to the neighbors.
They take a basket and fill it with eggs from the hen house. They are careful not to break them. They walk along the road and knock on the doors. They say hello and give the eggs to the people. The people are happy and thank them.
On their way back, they see a big puddle. It looks fun to jump in. Tom says, "Let's play in the puddle!" Sue says, "But what about the eggs? They will get dirty." Tom says, "It doesn't matter. They are in the basket. Come on, it will be fun!"
They put the basket on the ground and run to the puddle. They jump and splash and laugh. They get wet and muddy. They forget about the eggs.
But then, a dog comes by. He sees the basket and smells the eggs. He is hungry and curious. He runs to the basket and knocks it over. The eggs fall out and break. The dog licks them up.
Tom and Sue hear the noise and turn around. They see the dog and the mess. They are shocked and sad. They say, "Oh no! The eggs! The dog ate them! What will we do?"
They run to the basket and try to save some eggs. But they are all dirty and broken. They cry and say, "We are sorry. We were bad. We should have been careful. We should not have played in the puddle. We wasted the eggs. We let the people down."
They go back to the farm and tell their parents what happened. Their parents are disappointed and angry. They say, "You were irresponsible and selfish. You did not do your job. You did not respect the eggs or the people. You have to learn from your mistake. You have to apologize and make up for it."
Tom and Sue feel ashamed and sorry. They say, "We are sorry. We made a mistake. We will apologize and make up for it. We will not play in the puddle again. We will be more careful and respectful. We will do our job better next time."
The moral of the story is: You have to be careful and respectful when you have a job to do. You have to think of the consequences of your actions. You have to be honest and responsible when you make a mistake. You have to learn from your mistake and try to improve.

The man looked at Jill and then at Tom. He saw that they were just kids who wanted to play. He felt sorry and angry.
"Sorry? You are sorry? You took my umbrella, my only shelter, and played with it like a toy. Do you know how hard it is to live on the street? Do you know how cold and wet it is at night? Do you know how hungry and lonely I am?" The man said.
He let go of Tom and pushed him to the ground. He picked up his umbrella and his bag and walked away. He muttered to himself and shook his head.
Jill and Tom were hurt and scared. They ran to each other and hugged. They cried and wished they had never seen the umbrella. They learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that some things are not toys, but necessities. They learned that some people are not happy, but sad. They learned that they should not take what is not theirs, but respect what is others'. They learned that playing can be fun, but also dangerous.

Lily liked to help her grandma in the garden. She watered the flowers, pulled the weeds, and picked the prunes. Prunes were purple and sweet and good for you. Grandma said they grew on the prune tree.
One day, Lily saw a bird on the prune tree. It was small and brown and had a red cap. It sang a pretty song. Lily wanted to say hello to the bird. She climbed on a stool and reached for a branch.
"Hello, bird," Lily said. "Do you like prunes?"
The bird looked at Lily and tilted its head. It flew to another branch and picked a prune with its beak. It ate the prune and sang again.
"Yes, I like prunes," the bird said. "They are yummy and juicy. Thank you for sharing."
Lily was surprised and happy. She had never talked to a bird before. She smiled and gave the bird another prune.
"You're welcome, bird," Lily said. "What is your name?"
The bird flew closer to Lily and pecked her cheek gently. It said, "My name is Ruby. I live in the woods. I come here sometimes to visit the prune tree. It is my favorite tree."
Lily hugged the bird and said, "My name is Lily. I live in the house. I come here every day to help my grandma. She is my favorite person."
Ruby and Lily became friends. They talked and played and shared prunes. They had a lot of fun. But soon, the sun was setting and the sky was getting dark.
"I have to go, Lily," Ruby said. "It is time for me to return to the woods. I have to find my nest and sleep."
Lily was sad. She did not want Ruby to leave. She said, "Will you come back, Ruby? Will you visit me again?"
Ruby nodded and said, "Of course, Lily. I will come back. You are my favorite person too. I will visit you whenever I can. But you have to promise me something."
Lily said, "What is it, Ruby?"
Ruby said, "You have to promise me to take care of the prune tree. It is our special tree. It gives us prunes and shade and happiness. It needs water and love and respect."
Lily said, "I promise, Ruby. I will take care of the prune tree. It is our special tree. I love it and you."

"Help! Help!" they screamed.

"Ben, this is your fault! You should have listened to me and questioned Mom!" said Lily.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should have been more careful and respectful," said Ben.

"Well, curiosity can be dangerous sometimes. You should always ask permission before entering someone else's place. And you should always respect their boundaries. Do you understand?" said Mr. Lee.
"Yes, Mr. Lee. We understand. We won't do it again. Thank you for saving us," said Ben and Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong horse named Max. Max loved to run and play in the fields all day long. One day, Max saw a butterfly and chased it all the way to a tree. The butterfly flew away, but Max saw a bird's nest with a knot in it.
Max said, "I can untie that knot with my powerful teeth!" But just as he was about to try, he heard a voice say, "Don't touch that knot, Max. It's holding the nest together."
Max turned around and saw a wise old owl sitting on a branch. "Why can't I untie the knot?" Max asked.
The owl replied, "Because if you do, the nest will fall apart and the baby birds will be hurt. Sometimes it's better to leave things as they are and not use your power to shut them down."
Max thought about what the owl said and realized that sometimes being powerful means knowing when to hold back. From that day on, Max ran and played with a new understanding of his strength.

But then they heard a loud crack. The snowman was standing on a frozen lake. The ice was thin and it broke under his weight. The snowman started to sink into the water. Tom and Lily were scared.
"Help! Help!" They shouted. They wanted to save their snowman, but they knew it was too dangerous to go on the ice.
Luckily, a man heard their cries. He came with a rope and a stick. He threw the rope to the snowman and told Tom and Lily to hold the other end. He used the stick to break the ice around the snowman. He pulled and pulled until the snowman was out of the water. He put him on the shore. He was wet and cold, but he was safe.
"Thank you, thank you!" Tom and Lily said to the man. They hugged their snowman and wrapped him in the scarf. They were very happy.
The man smiled and said, "You're welcome, kids. But be careful next time. Don't play on the icy lake. It's not safe."
Tom and Lily nodded and said, "We will. Thank you, sir."
They waved goodbye to the man and took their snowman home. They put him in their yard and gave him a new hat. They hoped he would stay for a long time. They loved their snowman.

The old woman sadly looked around and said, "Oh, my old friend... all of this space, it's so quiet and calm, but all the trees here seem so lonely and sad, where are all the birds, the sunlight, and the friendly wind?"
The tree smiled, and replied, "My dear, all of these things will return when it's time, until then, it is we who must yield wisdom and strength to the world. We must help keep this ancient space alive and beautiful, no matter how little or big we are."
The old woman smiled and said, "You are wise indeed, my old friend, thank you for your words and wisdom." 
The moral of the story is that even when things seem quiet and lonely, small acts of kindness will yield strength and wisdom and help make the world a better

The bunny said, "Thank you, train. I surrender. I will move now." The bunny and his friends moved away from the track. The train went on the track, happy to help the bunny and his friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big green park, lived a thin cat named Tom. Tom loved to play with a small ball. His goal was to deliver the ball to his friend, a cute dog named Max.
One day, Tom said to Max, "Let's play! I will deliver the ball to you, and you will catch it." Max wagged his tail and said, "Yes, let's play!"
Tom kicked the ball with his paw. The ball went up, up, up into the sky. Max ran fast to catch the ball. He jumped high and caught it in his mouth. He was so happy that he barked, "I did it! I caught the ball!"
Tom and Max played all day. They took turns delivering the ball and catching it. They laughed and had lots of fun. When the sun went down, they were tired but happy.
From that day on, Tom and Max played together every day. They became the best of friends. And Tom's thin legs grew strong from playing so much.

Inside, Tom saw many people in pretty clothes singing loud songs. He did not like the loud songs. Tom said to a man next to him, "I don't like the loud songs. Can we make them stop?" The man said, "No, we cannot. This is an opera. We must listen to the loud songs."
Tom was sad. He did not want to listen to the loud songs. He tried to leave, but the door was closed. He tried to open the door, but it was too hard. Tom was stuck inside the opera, listening to the loud songs. He was not happy at the fair anymore.

A few weeks later, the garden started to grow, and it was the most beautiful garden Lily had ever seen. But then, one morning, Lily woke up to find that all the flowers had been pulled out of the ground and thrown on the sidewalk. She was so sad and didn't understand why someone would do that.

Tim and Mia were squirrels who liked to play in the big park. They climbed trees, chased birds, and hid nuts for later. One day, they found a big sack under a bench. It was full of acorns!
"Wow, look at all these nuts!" Tim said. "We can take them to our nest and have a feast!"
"Or we can share them with our friends!" Mia said. "They would be happy to see us with such a big gift!"
Tim and Mia decided to share the acorns with their friends. They dragged the sack along the path, but it was very heavy. They stopped to rest near a pond.
"Are we there yet?" Tim asked. He was tired and thirsty.
"Not yet," Mia said. "We have to cross the bridge and go up the hill. Then we will see our friends' tree. It is very distant, but we can do it!"
As they were resting, they heard a loud bark. A big dog was running towards them. It saw the sack and wanted to play with it.
"Uh-oh, a dog!" Tim said. "We have to run!"
"Leave the sack!" Mia said. "It is too slow!"
But Tim did not want to leave the sack. He liked the acorns too much. He tried to pull the sack away from the dog, but the dog was stronger. It bit the sack and tore it open. Acorns spilled everywhere.
"Tim, come on!" Mia said. "The dog will catch you!"
Tim realized he had made a mistake. He let go of the sack and ran after Mia. They escaped the dog and climbed a nearby tree. They were safe, but they had lost the acorns.
"I'm sorry, Mia," Tim said. "I was greedy and foolish. I should have listened to you."
"It's okay, Tim," Mia said. "We still have each other. And we can find more acorns later. Maybe not as many, but enough."
They hugged and looked at the distant tree where their friends lived. They hoped they would understand and forgive them. They learned a lesson that day: sharing is better than hoarding, and friendship is more valuable than nuts.

Lily was angry and sad. She did not like Ben. She thought he was mean and selfish. She decided to try one more time. She got a chair from the kitchen and put it on the couch. She climbed on the chair and reached for the ball.
But the chair was not stable. It wobbled and tipped over. Lily lost her balance and fell down. The ball also fell down and hit her head. Lily cried out loud. She was hurt and scared.
Ben heard Lily's cry and ran to her. He saw the blood on her forehead and the ball on the floor. He felt sorry and guilty. He hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily, I should have helped you. Are you okay?"
Lily stopped crying and looked at Ben. She saw his worried face and heard his kind words. She forgave him and said, "It's okay, Ben, I should have listened to you. The ball was dangerous. Can we play together?"
Ben nodded and smiled. He got a band-aid from the bathroom and put it on Lily's wound. He said, "Yes, Lily, let's play together. But not with the ball. Let's play with something else."
They put the ball back on the shelf and picked up their toys. They played nicely and happily. They did not fight or ignore each other. They had peace and love.

Lena encourages Ben. She says, "Don't be afraid, Ben. We can make the dragon together. It will be easy and fun. And the dragon will not bite us. It will be our friend. We can make it lively and friendly. We can give it a name and a smile. Come on, Ben. Let's make a dragon."
Ben smiles. He says, "OK, Lena. Let's make a dragon. What name should we give it?"
Lena thinks. She says, "How about Fluffy? Fluffy the friendly dragon."
Ben likes the name. He says, "Fluffy is a good name. Let's make Fluffy the friendly dragon."
They get some cardboard, scissors, tape and crayons. They cut out a big body, a long tail, a round head, two wings and four legs. They tape them together and color them green. They draw eyes, a nose, a mouth and some scales. They make Fluffy look lively and friendly.
They are proud of their cardboard dragon. They play with Fluffy. They pretend to be knights and princesses and go on adventures with Fluffy. They have a lot of fun with their cardboard dragon. They encourage each other to use their imagination and creativity. They are happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They had a big jug of water and some cups. They wanted to make tea for their toys.
"Here you go, Teddy. Some nice tea for you," Lily said. She poured some water from the jug into a cup and gave it to her teddy bear.
"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind," Ben said. He pretended to be the voice of the teddy bear.
Lily smiled. She liked playing with Ben. He was her best friend.
They heard a noise. It was Lily's mom. She was coming out of the house.
"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" she asked.
"We are making tea for our toys," Lily said.
"That's fun. Can I have some too?" her mom asked.
"Sure, mom. Here you go," Lily said. She poured some water from the jug into another cup and gave it to her mom.
Her mom took a sip. She made a funny face.
"Oops. This tea is very cold. And salty. Did you use water from the hose?" she asked.
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They nodded. They had used water from the hose. They thought it was the same as water from the tap.
They felt embarrassed. They did not know that water from the hose was not good for drinking.
They saw their mom smile. She was not angry. She was just teasing them.
She put down the cup and hugged them.
"It's okay, kids. I know you were trying to be nice. But next time, use water from the tap, okay? It's better for you and your toys," she said.
"Okay, mom. We are sorry," Lily and Ben said.
They hugged their mom back. They were happy. They loved their mom.
They waved to their mom as she went back into the house. They decided to play something else. They had a lot of fun in the garden.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy animals on the floor. They had a big elephant, a small mouse, a loud lion and a quiet rabbit. Lily liked the elephant best, because it was big and strong. Ben liked the mouse best, because it was small and fast.
"Let's weigh our animals," Lily said. "I bet my elephant is the heaviest."
"Okay," Ben said. "How do we weigh them?"
Lily thought for a moment. She saw a big book on the table. She got up and dragged the book to the floor. "We can use this book as a scale," she said. "We put one animal on each side and see which side goes down."
They put the elephant on one side of the book and the mouse on the other side. The book tilted down on the elephant's side. "See, my elephant is heavier than your mouse," Lily said.
"Let's try another pair," Ben said. He took the lion and the rabbit and put them on the book. The book tilted down on the lion's side. "My lion is heavier than your rabbit," Ben said.
They tried all the pairs of animals and saw which ones were heavier and which ones were lighter. They had fun comparing their animals and making noises like them.
Then they heard a gentle voice from the door. It was their mom. "What are you two doing?" she asked.
"We are weighing our animals, mom," Lily said. "We are using this book as a scale."
"That's very clever," mom said. "But it's time for a snack now. Come and wash your hands."
Lily and Ben put their animals back in their basket and followed mom to the kitchen. They were hungry and happy. They liked playing with their animals and learning new things.

Tom and Sue wanted to go on the water in a kayak. A kayak is a long boat that you sit in and move with a stick that has a flat part on each end. They asked their dad if they could borrow his kayak, and he said yes, but they had to be careful and not spoil it.
They took the kayak to the lake and put it in the water. They put on life jackets and got in the kayak. They had fun paddling around and looking at the fish and the birds. They saw another kayak with two kids in it. The kids waved at them and said hello.
"Hi, do you want to race?" one of the kids asked.
"Sure, we like to race!" Tom said.
"OK, let's go to that big rock over there and back. Ready, set, go!" the other kid said.
Tom and Sue paddled as fast as they could, but the other kayak was faster. They got to the rock first and turned around. Tom and Sue tried to catch up, but they were too far behind.
"Ha ha, we win, we win!" the other kids shouted.
They were so happy that they did not see a big branch sticking out of the water. They hit the branch with their kayak and made a big hole in it. Water started to get in the kayak and make it sink.
"Help, help, we're sinking!" the other kids cried.
Tom and Sue saw what happened and paddled to them. They helped them get out of the kayak and onto the shore. They were wet and scared, but not hurt.
"Thank you, thank you, you saved us!" the other kids said.
"You're welcome, but what about your kayak? It's spoiled now. How will you tell your dad?" Sue asked.
The other kids looked at the kayak and started to cry.
"We don't know, we don't know. We were ignorant. We did not look where we were going. We were too busy showing off. We're sorry, we're sorry!" they said.
Tom and Sue felt sorry for them, but they also felt glad that they did not spoil their dad's kayak. They learned a lesson that day: it is better to be careful and kind than to be fast and rude.

Jen says, "Ha ha! My truck is just right and quiet! It can deliver anything gentle!"

Ben did not like cauliflower. It was white and hard and had a bad smell. He pushed it away on his plate and made a face.
"Ben, you have to eat your cauliflower. It is good for you," his mom said.
"No, mom, I don't want it. It is yucky," Ben said.
"Please, Ben, just try one bite. If you don't eat it, you can't have dessert," his mom said.
Ben looked at the dessert. It was a big slice of chocolate cake with cream and sprinkles. He wanted it very much. But he did not want the cauliflower.
He had an idea. He took a big spoon and scooped up some cauliflower. He pretended to put it in his mouth, but he really hid it under his napkin. He did this again and again until his plate was empty.
"See, mom, I ate all my cauliflower. Can I have cake now?" he said.
His mom smiled and gave him a piece of cake. Ben was happy. He ate the cake and licked his fingers. It was sweet and soft and had a good taste.
But then he felt something cold and wet on his lap. He looked down and saw his napkin. It was full of cauliflower and it had fallen off his plate. The cauliflower was cold and soggy and had a worse smell.
His mom saw it too. She was not happy. She took away his cake and said, "Ben, you lied to me. You did not eat your cauliflower. You hid it under your napkin. That is not nice. You have to leave the table and go to your room. No more cake for you."
Ben was sad. He cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I don't like cauliflower. Please, can I have some cake?"
But his mom said, "No, Ben. You have to learn your lesson. Maybe next time you will eat your cauliflower. Now go to your room and think about what you did."
Ben left the table and went to his room. He wished he had eaten his cauliflower. He wished he had not lied to his mom. He wished he had some cake. He did not like cauliflower. But he liked cake. And he liked his mom. He hoped she would forgive him. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you."

The careful potato felt sad and said sorry to the mad potato. It promised to be more careful next time. The mad potato forgave the careful potato and they both became friends again. In the end, all the potatoes had a fun time at the party and the careful potato was very shiny.

Benny felt sad, but he remembered what the wise old owl had told him. He rubbed his feet and jogged over to his friends. They were surprised to see him running so fast and asked him how he did it. Benny told them about rubbing his feet before jogging. His friends tried it too and they all had fun playing together. Benny learned that he could be independent and solve his own problems by asking for help and trying new things.

Max looked at Sam and saw tiny black dots on his fur. He knew what they were. They were fleas. Fleas were bad bugs that bit and made you itch. Max did not like fleas. He had them once, and he had to take a bath with soap and water. He hated baths.
"Sam, you have fleas," he meowed. "You need to take a bath to get rid of them."
Sam did not like the sound of that. He hated baths too. He liked to be dirty and smelly. He thought baths were for cats, not dogs. He shook his head and backed away.
"No, no, no, I don't want a bath!" he barked. "There must be another way!"

"Sam, I know you don't like baths, but they are the only way to get rid of the fleas. Trust me, it will make you feel better. I will help you. I will find some soap and a towel and a brush. "I promise, Sam, I will play with you afterwards. Come on, let's go. The sooner we start, the sooner we finish."

They chase the dog and shout at him. The dog is wild and fast. He runs around the park and makes a lot of noise. He does not listen to Tim and Sam. He thinks it is a fun game.
But then he sees a cat. He drops the ball and the hoop and runs after the cat. The cat is scared and climbs a tree. The dog barks at the cat and tries to climb too. But he is too big and falls down.
Tim and Sam see their ball and their hoop on the ground. They are happy and run to get them. They say thank you to the cat and bye to the dog. They go back to their spot and play with their ball and their hoop. They have fun and forget about the wild dog.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play with cars and dolls. One day, they find a big loop in the park. It is made of metal and has a hole in the middle.
"Wow, look at this loop!" Tom says. "It is so big and shiny!"
"Can we play with it?" Anna asks. She is eager to try something new.
"I think we can," Tom says. "Maybe we can roll it or jump through it."
They take turns to roll the loop on the grass. It makes a loud noise and goes very fast. They laugh and clap their hands.
"Let me try to jump through it," Anna says. She runs and leaps into the hole. But she is too small and gets stuck.
"Help, help!" Anna cries. "I can't get out!"
Tom runs to her and tries to pull her out. But he is too weak and can't move the loop.
"Oh no, what can we do?" Tom says. He is scared and worried.
They hear a voice behind them. It is a man who works in the park. He sees them and comes to help.
"Hello, kids, what are you doing here?" he asks. "This loop is not a toy. It is for a sculpture."
"We are sorry, sir," Tom says. "We just wanted to play with it. But Anna got stuck and we can't get her out."
"Don't worry, I will help you," the man says. He is kind and strong. He lifts the loop and frees Anna. She is happy and hugs Tom.
"Thank you, sir," Anna says. "You are very nice."
"You are welcome, kids," the man says. "But next time, be careful and don't play with things that are not yours. They might be dangerous or break."
"We understand, sir," Tom says. "We will be more careful and ask before we play."
They say goodbye to the man and go back to their cars and dolls. They are still friends and still like to play. But they also think before they do.

When the plate was revealed, everyone was impressed. It was the most beautiful plate! Papa said that the plate was specially made to remind the family that they should not quarrel. He said that whenever they argued, they should look at the plate and remember to remain peaceful instead.
The plan worked! The family was so impressed by the plate that it reminded them of their special bond every time they argued. They learned to get along better and the quarrelling stopped. The plate was an impressive reminder that family should always stay together.

But today it was feeling extra brave, so it decided to climb the tree again. Even though the small herb was scared, it made it all the way to the top. Eventually, it came back down to the ground, safe and proud of its adventure.

After a while, the lazy trail had had enough naps. It slowly began getting up and soon it was wide awake. The critter and the trail watched the sunrise together, and the trail was no longer lazy.

"Beep, beep!"

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to jog in the park. They jog fast and slow, and have fun. One day, they see a big sign. The sign says: "Jog Race. Win a prize. Sign up here."
Tim and Sam want to join the race. They sign up and get a number. Tim gets number one. Sam gets number two. They are happy and excited.
The race starts. Tim and Sam jog with many other people. Some people are big, some are small. Some people are fast, some are slow. Tim and Sam try to jog faster than everyone. They want to win the prize.
But then, Tim sees a girl. The girl is unique. She has a pink hat, a purple shirt, and a green skirt. She also has a big smile. Tim likes the girl. He slows down and says: "Hi, I am Tim. What is your name?"
The girl says: "Hi, I am Kim. I like your number. It is one. One is my favorite number."
Tim and Kim jog together. They talk and laugh. They forget about the race. They are happy.
Sam sees Tim and Kim. He is surprised. He thinks: "Why is Tim talking to the girl? He should jog faster. He should try to win the prize."
Sam jogs faster. He passes many people. He sees the finish line. He thinks: "I am going to win. I am going to get the prize."
But then, Sam sees a boy. The boy is unique. He has a blue hat, a yellow shirt, and a red pants. He also has a big smile. Sam likes the boy. He slows down and says: "Hi, I am Sam. What is your number?"
The boy says: "Hi, I am Jim. I like your number. It is two. Two is my favorite number."
Sam and Jim jog together. They talk and laugh. They forget about the race. They are happy.
Tim and Kim, and Sam and Jim, jog to the finish line. They are the last ones. They do not win the prize. But they do not care. They have made new friends. They have had fun. They have completed the race.
The moral of the story is: It is not always important to win. Sometimes, it is more important to enjoy the journey and make new friends.

"Can we ride them, mom?" Lily asked.
"Not today, sweetie. They are too big and fast for you. Maybe when you are older, you can ride them with me," their mom replied.
Lily and Ben nodded, but they still wanted to ride the horses. They thought they looked so fun and strong. They decided to wait until their mom was busy with something else, and then sneak into the barn and try to ride them.
They waited until their mom went to the chicken coop to collect the eggs. Then they ran to the barn and climbed on the fence. They saw the horses eating hay and drinking water. They looked for the smallest and gentlest one. They thought it was Daisy, because she had a white spot on her nose and a pink ribbon on her mane.
"Let's ride Daisy," Ben whispered to Lily.
"OK, but be careful," Lily whispered back.
They jumped off the fence and walked slowly towards Daisy. They tried to pet her and talk to her softly. Daisy seemed friendly and let them touch her. Lily and Ben smiled and climbed on her back. They held on to her ribbon and said, "Giddy up, Daisy!"
Daisy was surprised and scared by the sudden weight and noise on her back. She did not like it at all. She shook her head and neighed loudly. She started to run and buck, trying to get rid of Lily and Ben. Lily and Ben screamed and held on tight, but they could not control Daisy. She ran out of the barn and into the field, where the other horses were grazing.
Their mom heard the commotion and looked up. She saw Daisy running wild with Lily and Ben on her back. She dropped the eggs and ran after them, calling their names. She was very worried and angry. She hoped they would not fall off and get hurt.
She caught up with Daisy and grabbed her reins. She stopped her and calmed her down. She helped Lily and Ben get off her back. She hugged them and checked if they were OK. They were not hurt, but they were very scared and sorry.
"Why did you do that, Lily and Ben? You know you are not supposed to ride the horses without me. You could have been hurt or lost. You scared Daisy and me. You were very naughty," their mom said.

"I'm sorry, mom," Lily said.
"Me too, mom," Ben said.
Their mom sighed and said, "I'm glad you are sorry, but you have to learn to follow the rules. The horses are not toys. They are living creatures that need respect and care. You have to be gentle and careful with them. And you have to do what I tell you, because I love you and I want you to be safe."
Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We understand, mom. We love you too."

Sara loved to look at the flowers in the garden. She liked how they had different colors and shapes. She liked how they smelled sweet and fresh. She liked how they made her feel happy and comfortable.
One day, she saw a new flower in the garden. It was big and purple and had many petals. It looked like a star. Sara wanted to touch it and smell it. She walked towards it and reached out her hand.
"Hello, little girl," a voice said. Sara was surprised. She looked around and saw a stranger. He was a man with a hat and a coat. He had a big smile and a bag. He was standing behind the fence.
"Who are you?" Sara asked. She felt scared and curious.
"I'm a friend," the stranger said. "I like flowers too. Do you want to see what I have in my bag? I have some very special flowers. They are more beautiful than the ones in your garden. They can bloom all year round. They can make you very happy. Do you want to come with me and see them?"
Sara thought for a moment. She liked flowers very much. She wanted to see the special flowers. But she also remembered what her mom and dad had told her. They had told her not to talk to strangers. They had told her to stay in the garden. They had told her to be careful and smart.
"No, thank you," Sara said. "I like the flowers in my garden. They are enough for me. They are my friends. They make me comfortable. I don't want to go with you. You are a stranger. You are not my friend. Goodbye."

"Because we found a big magnet in the garage," Mia said. "It was so interesting!"
Mom looked at the fridge. She saw the big magnet and the other magnets on it. She did not see the note.
"Where is the note I left you?" mom asked.
Tom and Mia looked at the fridge. They did not see the note. They wondered where it was.
Mom looked under the table. She saw the note on the floor. She picked it up and showed it to Tom and Mia.
"Here is the note," mom said. "It says: Don't forget to wash your hands before eating. The big magnet made the note fall off. The big magnet did not remind you to wash your hands. It made you forget."
Tom and Mia felt sorry. They said sorry to mom. They went to the bathroom and washed their hands. They learned that magnets are interesting, but they are not good at reminding.

Jen and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big bunch of grapes on a bench. They were hungry and wanted to eat them.
"Can we have some grapes?" Jen asked.
"Let's ask the lady first," Tom said. He saw a lady sitting on another bench, reading a book. He thought she might be the owner of the grapes.
Tom walked to the lady and said, "Excuse me, are these your grapes?"
The lady looked up and smiled. "No, they are not. I found them here too. Someone must have left them by mistake. You can have them if you want."
"Thank you, lady!" Tom said. He ran back to Jen with the grapes.
"Yay, we can have grapes!" Jen said. She took a small grape and put it in her mouth. It was sweet and juicy. She liked it a lot.
"Me too!" Tom said. He took a small grape and ate it. He liked it too.
They ate more grapes and shared them with the lady. They were happy and full.
But then, something bad happened. Jen felt a tickle in her throat. She started to cough. She could not breathe well.
"Jen, are you okay?" Tom asked. He was scared.
"I don't know. I can't breathe. Help!" Jen said.
The lady heard them and came over. She saw Jen's face. It was red and swollen.
"Oh no, she is allergic to grapes!" the lady said. She took out her phone and called for help.
"Repeat, repeat, I need help! A child is allergic to grapes! We are in the park, near the fountain. Hurry, please!" the lady said.
Soon, a big truck with a red cross came. Some people in white clothes got out. They had a bag with a needle and a tube. They gave Jen the needle and the tube. They helped her breathe.
Jen felt better. She stopped coughing. Her face was normal again.
"Thank you, thank you!" Jen said.
"You're welcome, sweetie. You're very brave," one of the people in white said.
They took Jen and Tom to the hospital. The lady went with them. She gave them a hug and a kiss.
"I'm sorry, I didn't know you were allergic to grapes. I hope you feel better soon," the lady said.
"It's okay, lady. You were very nice to us. Thank you for sharing your grapes and calling for help," Tom said.
Jen nodded. She smiled.
They learned a lesson. They learned to be careful with new foods. They learned to repeat, repeat, if they need help. They learned to be grateful for friends and helpers.
They were still friends. They still liked to play in the park. But they never ate grapes again.

His mom said, "I do love you, Tommy, but I also want you to be smart and helpful. You have to earn your privileges. This is your last chance. Do your homework and clean your room, or no cartoons for a week."
Tommy still did not listen. He said, "Fine, mom, I do not care. I will watch cartoons anyway. You cannot stop me."

But his mom followed him. She saw him watching cartoons. She was very sad and angry. She said, "Tommy, you disobeyed me. You did not do your homework and clean your room. You did not accept the consequences. You are in big trouble."

Tommy was shocked and scared. He realized his mom was serious. He realized he made a big mistake. He realized he hurt his mom's feelings. He felt sorry and ashamed.
He said, "Mom, I am sorry. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. I should have done my homework and cleaned my room. I should have accepted your decision. I was selfish and lazy. Please forgive me. Please let me watch cartoons again."

You have to accept that you cannot watch cartoons for a week. You have to prove that you can be smart and helpful. You have to earn your privileges back. Do you understand?"
Tommy said, "Yes, mom, I understand. I will do my homework and clean my room. I will accept that I cannot watch cartoons for a week. I will prove that I can be smart and helpful. I will earn my privileges back. I love you, mom."
His mom said, "I love you too, Tommy. I am proud of you for admitting your mistake and trying to fix it. I hope you learned your lesson. I hope you will be more respectful and responsible from now on. I hope you will enjoy your cartoons more when you deserve them."
Tommy nodded and hugged his mom. He went to his room and did his homework and cleaned his room. He felt better and happier. He learned his lesson. He learned that he had to accept the consequences of his actions. He learned that he had to do what he needed to do before he did what he wanted to do. He learned that he had to be smart and helpful to be happy. He learned that he had to love his mom and respect her rules. He learned that cartoons were more fun when he earned them. He learned that being a good boy was better than being a selfish and lazy boy. He learned a lot from his mom and his cartoons.

Mom hears them and comes to their room. She sees them fighting over the red sock. She says, "Stop it, both of you. That is not a toy. That is a sock. And it is not yours. It is mine. I lost it when I did the laundry. Now, remove it from your hand and give it to me."
Lily and Ben are surprised. They look at the red sock. They see that it has a hole in it. They feel silly. They remove the sock from their hand and give it to Mom. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We did not know. We thought it was our sock."

Lily and Ben nod. They say, "Okay, Mom. We will play with our blocks. And we will share and be nice." They hug Mom and then go to their toy box. They find their blocks and start to build a tower. They smile and laugh. They forget about the red sock.

But then, a big dog came running to the park. He saw the mud castle and thought it was a toy. He jumped on it and smashed it with his paws. He barked and wagged his tail.

"Go away, bad dog!" Lily cried. "You are not nice!"
The dog did not listen. He kept playing with the mud. Ben and Lily were very sad and angry. They wanted to restore their mud castle, but it was too late. It was all broken and messy.
Then, a man came to the park. He saw the dog and the mud castle. He was the dog's owner. He called the dog and put a leash on him.
"I'm sorry, kids," he said. "My dog did not mean to hurt your mud castle. He just wanted to play. He does not know better."
Ben and Lily looked at the man and the dog. They were still upset, but they also felt sorry for the dog. He looked happy and friendly. He did not know he did something wrong.
"It's okay, mister," Ben said. "We know your dog is not bad. He just likes mud."

"Thank you, mister," Ben and Lily said. "You are very good at making mud castles!"
"You're welcome, kids," the man said. "You are very good at sharing and forgiving. You are very good kids!"
The moral value of the story is: Sometimes, things go wrong and people make mistakes, but we can restore them with kindness and understanding.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved Christmas. They always helped their mom and dad decorate the house with lights and a big tree. They also wrote letters to Santa and put them in a red envelope. They wanted to ask Santa how he came to their house and gave them presents.
On Christmas Eve, they put on their pajamas and brushed their teeth. They also left some cookies and milk for Santa and some carrots for his reindeer. They went to their bedroom and tried to sleep, but they were too excited. They whispered to each other in the dark.
"Tom, do you think Santa will come soon?" Lily asked.
"I don't know, Lily. Maybe he is very busy with other kids," Tom said.
"How does he get in our house? We don't have a chimney," Lily said.
Tom thought for a moment. He remembered what his dad told him once.
"Dad said Santa has a magic key that can open any door. He also said Santa is very quiet and fast, so we don't hear him," Tom explained.
"Wow, that's amazing. I wish I could see him," Lily said.
"Me too, but we have to be asleep or he won't come. He knows if we are awake or not," Tom said.
They closed their eyes and tried to sleep. They dreamed of Santa and his sleigh and the presents they hoped to get.
Meanwhile, outside their house, Santa parked his sleigh on the roof. He took out his magic key and opened the door. He tiptoed inside and saw the cookies and milk and the carrots. He smiled and ate some of them. He also saw the red envelope with the letters from Tom and Lily. He opened it and read their questions. He decided to write them a note and put it in the envelope. He wrote:
Dear Tom and Lily,
Thank you for your lovely letters and the treats. I am happy to answer your questions. I use a magic key to get in houses that don't have a chimney. I am very quiet and fast, so you don't hear me. I also have a special bag that can hold all the presents for all the kids in the world. I hope you like the ones I brought you. They are under the tree. You are very good twins and I am proud of you. Merry Christmas and sweet dreams.
Love, Santa
He put the note in the envelope and placed it on the table. He then put the presents under the tree and checked his list. He saw that Tom and Lily were asleep and he winked at them. He went back to the door and locked it with his magic key. He climbed on his sleigh and flew away. He shouted:
"Ho ho ho! Merry Christmas to all and to all a good night!"
Tom and Lily woke up in the morning and ran to the living room. They saw the presents and the note from Santa. They opened the note and read it. They were amazed and happy. They hugged each other and said:
"Santa is real and he is awesome!"
They opened their presents and played with them. They also thanked their mom and dad for the warm and cozy Christmas. They had a wonderful day.

"OK," Ben said. "That sounds fun. But we have to be fair and take turns."
They shuffled the cards and put them face down on the floor. Lily went first and picked a card. It had a blue rocket on it.

Tom and Sue nod, but they do not listen. They sneak into the kitchen and eat all the cookies. They do not leave any for their friends.
Mom comes back and sees the empty box. She is very angry. She says, "Tom and Sue, you are very bad. You ate all the cookies and did not share. You wasted the food and hurt your friends. You have to say sorry and pray for forgiveness."
Tom and Sue feel sorry. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We were greedy and wasteful. We hurt our friends. We will pray for forgiveness. Please do not be mad at us."
Mom hugs them and says, "I love you, but you have to learn to share and be kind. Next time, think of others before you take. Pray to God and ask him to help you be good."

Tim and Mia were playing in the farm. They liked to run and jump in the wide field of wheat. The wheat was tall and yellow and made a nice sound when the wind blew.
"Look, Tim, a big red barn!" Mia said, pointing to a wooden building. "Let's go and see what's inside!"
They ran to the barn and opened the door. They saw many animals: cows, pigs, chickens, and a horse. They also saw a big machine with a funnel and a wheel.
"What is that?" Tim asked, curious.
"That is a mill," a voice said. It was the farmer, who was working on the machine. "It makes flour from wheat. Do you want to see how it works?"
"Yes, please!" Tim and Mia said, excited.
The farmer smiled and picked up a handful of wheat. He poured it into the funnel and turned the wheel. The wheat went down and came out as white powder.
"Wow, that's amazing!" Mia said. "The wheat shrank and changed!"
"That's right," the farmer said. "The mill grinds the wheat and makes it into flour. Then we can use the flour to bake bread and cakes and pies. Do you like bread and cakes and pies?"
"Yes, we do!" Tim and Mia said, hungry.
"Then come with me," the farmer said. "I have some fresh ones in the kitchen. You can have a slice if you like."
Tim and Mia followed the farmer to the kitchen. They smelled the delicious aroma of baked goods. They thanked the farmer and enjoyed a slice of bread and cake and pie. They learned a lot about wheat and flour and mill. They had a fun and tasty day at the farm.

Tom and Lily wanted to make a cake for Mom. They found a big bowl and some things to put in it. They saw a spoon and a shiny object on the table. Tom said, "Let's use this to stir the cake." He picked up the shiny object. It was a knife.
Lily said, "No, Tom, that is not a spoon. That is a knife. It can hurt you. Put it down." But Tom did not listen. He said, "I can stir with a knife. It is fun. Look, it makes lines in the cake." He stirred the bowl with the knife.
Lily saw that the oven was on. She said, "Tom, the oven is hot. We have to be careful. Mom said not to touch the oven." But Tom did not listen. He said, "I want to put the cake in the oven. It will be yummy. I can do it by myself." He lifted the bowl with the knife.
Lily tried to stop him. She said, "Tom, no, you will drop the cake. You will burn yourself. Let me help you." But Tom did not listen. He said, "Go away, Lily. I can do it. I am big." He walked to the oven with the bowl and the knife.
Lily watched in horror. Tom tripped on the rug. He dropped the bowl and the knife. The cake splashed on the floor. The knife cut his hand. The oven door hit his head. He screamed in pain. Lily ran to him. She cried for help. Mom heard the noise. She came to the kitchen. She saw the mess and the blood. She was very angry and very scared. She called the doctor. She said, "Tom, what have you done? You are very naughty and very silly. You could have died." Tom felt very sorry and very hurt. He wished he had listened to Lily. He wished he had used a spoon.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to jump and run and catch bugs. They saw a big frog near the pond. It was green and wet and had big eyes.
"Look, a frog!" Lily said. "Let's catch it!"
They ran to the frog and tried to grab it. But the frog was fast and smart. It sprang away from their hands and hopped into the water.
"Hey, come back!" Ben said. "We want to play with you!"
They followed the frog to the pond and looked for it. They saw it hiding under a leaf. They reached for it again. But the frog sprang out of the water and landed on Lily's head.
"Ah!" Lily screamed. "Get it off me!"
She shook her head and the frog fell to the ground. It sprang away again and disappeared into the grass.
Lily and Ben were sad and angry. They wanted the frog to be their friend. They sat on the edge of the pond and pouted.
"Stupid frog," Ben said. "Why did it do that?"
"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it was scared of us."
"Or maybe it was hungry," Ben said. "Maybe it wanted a meal."
They looked at each other and had an idea. They ran to the kitchen and got some bread and cheese. They came back to the garden and looked for the frog. They found it near a flower. It was still green and wet and had big eyes.
"Hello, frog," Lily said. "We are sorry we scared you. We brought you some food. Do you want some?"
They put the bread and cheese on the ground and moved back. The frog looked at them and the food. It was curious and hungry. It sprang to the food and ate some. It liked it. It made a croak.
"Thank you, kids," the frog said. "That was a good meal. You are nice."
Lily and Ben smiled. They were happy. The frog was happy too. It was not scared of them anymore. It was their friend.
They played with the frog for a while. They gave it a name. They called it Pale. Because it was not as green as the other frogs. It was a pale frog. But it was a special frog. And they loved it.

But Sam did not listen. He wanted to see the seal up close. He ran to the water and dove in. He swam fast and reached the rock. He smiled at the seal and said, "Hi, seal, I'm Sam. Do you want to play?"
The seal did not smile back. It did not want to play. It was angry and scared. It opened its mouth and showed its sharp teeth. It bit Sam's arm and made him bleed. Sam screamed and cried. He was hurt and scared.
Mia saw what happened and ran to get Mom and Dad. They came quickly and pulled Sam out of the water. They wrapped his arm with a cloth and took him to the car. They drove to the hospital to get help.
Sam was sorry he did not listen to Mom. He learned a hard lesson. He never dove near a wild seal again.

Lily liked to own potatoes. She had many potatoes in her room. She liked to play with them and make them talk. She gave them names and faces. She was happy with her potatoes.
One day, her big brother Tom came into her room. He was mean and angry. He saw Lily's potatoes and laughed. He said, "What are these? These are not toys. These are food. You are silly and stupid. I will take your potatoes and eat them."
Lily was fearful. She loved her potatoes. She did not want Tom to take them. She said, "No, Tom, no! These are my potatoes. They are my friends. Please leave them alone. Please go away."
But Tom did not listen. He grabbed Lily's potatoes and ran out of the room. He went to the kitchen and put them in a big pot. He filled the pot with water and turned on the fire. He said, "I will make potato soup. It will be yummy. And you will have no potatoes left."
Lily ran after Tom. She saw him cooking her potatoes. She cried and screamed. She tried to stop him. But it was too late. The potatoes were boiling and bubbling. They were soft and mushy. They were not her friends anymore. They were soup.
Tom laughed and poured the soup into a bowl. He said, "Here, Lily, have some soup. It is good for you. It is made from your potatoes. You should thank me."
Lily was sad and angry. She did not want soup. She wanted her potatoes. She pushed the bowl away. She said, "No, Tom, no! You are bad and mean. You hurt my potatoes. You hurt me. I hate you."
Tom shrugged and ate the soup. He said, "Too bad for you. More soup for me. You are a baby and a fool. You should grow up and stop playing with potatoes."
Lily ran away. She went to her room and cried. She had no potatoes left. She had no friends left. She was alone and unhappy. She wished she had her potatoes back. She wished Tom would go away. She wished she could own potatoes again. But she could not. The end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were pirates and look for treasure. They had a map that they drew with crayons and a shovel that they borrowed from the sandbox.
"Arrr, matey, we have to find the X on the map. That's where the treasure is," Tom said, holding the map in his hand.
"OK, captain, let's go," Lily said, following Tom with the shovel. They walked around the park, looking for clues. They saw a big tree, a slide, a bench, and a pond.
"Look, captain, there's the X!" Lily shouted, pointing to a spot near the pond. "It's under the rocks."
"Good job, matey, let's dig it up," Tom said, running to the rocks. He used the shovel to move the rocks away. He saw something shiny under the dirt.
"Wow, captain, what is it?" Lily asked, joining Tom.
Tom pulled out the shiny thing. It was a necklace with a big star on it. It sparkled in the sun.
"It's a star necklace. It must be very old and very precious. We found the treasure, matey. We are rich pirates now," Tom said, putting the necklace around his neck.
"Yay, captain, we did it. We are rich pirates now," Lily said, clapping her hands.
They hugged and danced around the pond. They were very happy.
But then they heard a voice.
"Hey, you two, what are you doing with my necklace?" the voice said.
They turned around and saw a lady. She looked angry. She was wearing a hat and a coat. She had a bag with her.
"That's my necklace. I lost it here yesterday. It's very important to me. It was a gift from my grandma. Give it back to me, now," the lady said, walking towards them.
Tom and Lily were scared. They did not know the lady. They did not know the necklace was hers. They thought they found the treasure.
"Sorry, lady, we did not know. We were playing pirates. We thought we found the treasure. We did not mean to take your necklace," Tom said, taking off the necklace and giving it to the lady.
"Yeah, sorry, lady, we were just playing. We did not want to make you sad," Lily said, nodding her head.
The lady took the necklace and looked at it. She smiled.
"Thank you, kids, for giving it back to me. I'm sorry I was angry. I was very worried. This necklace is very special to me. It reminds me of my grandma. She was a pirate too, you know," the lady said, winking at them.
"She was?" Tom and Lily asked, surprised.
"Yes, she was. She loved to travel and explore and have adventures. She gave me this necklace when I was a little girl. She told me it was a star to guide me in life. She was a good pirate, not a bad one," the lady said, touching the necklace.
"Wow, that's amazing. Your grandma sounds very cool. We like pirates too. We like to pretend we are pirates and look for treasure," Tom said, smiling.
"We do. We have a map and a shovel and everything," Lily said, showing the lady.
The lady looked at the map and the shovel. She laughed.
"That's very creative. You are very smart and brave pirates. I'm sure you will find many treasures in life. But remember, the best treasures are not always shiny and sparkly. Sometimes they are people and memories and love. Those are the treasures that make you rich, not poor," the lady said, hugging them.
"Thank you, lady. You are very nice and wise. You are a treasure too," Tom and Lily said, hugging her back.
They all smiled and said goodbye. Tom and Lily went back to their parents. The lady went back to her home. They all felt happy and rich. They all had treasures in their hearts.

Lily was a dog who liked to run and play in the park. She had a lot of friends, like Ben the cat, Sam the squirrel and Max the bird. They always had fun together, chasing balls, climbing trees and singing songs.
One day, Lily felt something itchy on her fur. She scratched and scratched, but it did not help. She looked and saw a tiny bug on her back. It was a flea. The flea was very hungry and bit Lily hard. Lily yelped and shook her fur, but the flea did not fall off.
"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" Lily cried. "Who are you and why are you hurting me?"
The flea laughed and said, "I am Fred, the most intelligent flea in the world. I have traveled to many places and learned many things. I can speak any language, solve any puzzle and tell any joke. And I am hungry, so I need to lend some of your blood."
Lily did not like Fred at all. She did not think he was intelligent, she thought he was mean and rude. She did not want to lend him her blood, she wanted him to leave her alone. She asked her friends for help.
"Ben, Sam, Max, please help me. There is a flea on my back who bites me and says he is intelligent. How can I get rid of him?"
Ben, Sam and Max looked at Lily and saw the flea. They did not like Fred either. They wanted to help Lily. They thought of a plan.
"Fred, if you are so intelligent, we have a challenge for you," Ben said. "We have a ball here that has a riddle on it. If you can read the riddle and answer it, we will let you stay on Lily. But if you cannot, you have to leave her alone. Do you accept?"
Fred was very confident. He thought he could read and answer any riddle. He agreed to the challenge. He jumped off Lily and landed on the ball. He looked at the riddle. It said:
What has four legs but does not walk?
Fred was puzzled. He tried to think of an answer, but he could not. He scratched his head and said, "I don't know. What is it?"
Ben, Sam and Max smiled and said, "A table!"
Fred felt very silly. He had failed the challenge. He had to leave Lily alone. He was ashamed and angry. He hopped off the ball and ran away.
Lily was very happy. She thanked her friends for helping her. She said, "You are the most intelligent and kind friends in the world. I am glad you are here."
They hugged and said, "You are welcome, Lily. We are glad you are here too."
They continued to play and have fun in the park, without any fleas.

Bob saw a little girl come to the ball. She turned off the alarm and counted the numbers on the ball. One, two, three. Bob was happy the alarm was off. The girl saw Bob under the tree and called him. Bob came out and played with the girl and the ball. They had a fun day together.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Mr. Smith. He was a teacher with many pupils in his class. One day, Mr. Smith asked a pupil named Tim to bring him a big red ball.
"Tim, can you bring me the big red ball?" Mr. Smith asked. Tim said, "Yes, Mr. Smith!" and went to find the ball. But Tim saw a big hole in the ground and thought it would be fun to hide the ball there.
The next day, Mr. Smith wanted to play a game with the big red ball. Tim remembered that he hid the ball in the big hole. He ran to the hole to get the ball, but it was gone! Tim was very sad.
Mr. Smith and the pupils looked for the ball, but they could not find it. They were all sad because they could not play the game. Tim wished he had not hid the ball in the hole. The end.

Tommy was a selfish boy. He did not like to share his toys or his snacks with his friends. He always wanted to have the best and the most of everything. One day, he saw a shiny new pair of shoes in the store window. They were red and blue and had lights on the bottom. Tommy wanted those shoes very much.
"Mommy, can I have those shoes?" he asked, pointing at the window.
"No, Tommy, you have enough shoes already. And those shoes are too expensive. We need to save money for other things," his mommy said.
"But I want them, I want them, I want them!" Tommy cried. He threw a tantrum in the store. He kicked and screamed and cried. His mommy was very angry and embarrassed. She dragged him out of the store and took him home. She put him in his room and told him to stay there until he calmed down.
Tommy was still very mad. He lay on his bed and pouted. He wished he had those shoes. He closed his eyes and dreamed about them. He dreamed that he was wearing them and running and jumping and flashing. He dreamed that everyone admired him and wanted to be his friend. He dreamed that he had all the shoes in the world and no one else had any.
But then, something strange happened in his dream. The shoes started to talk to him. They said, "Tommy, you are a selfish boy. You don't care about anyone but yourself. You don't share or help or say thank you. You only want more and more and more. You don't deserve us. We don't like you. We are going to leave you."
Tommy was scared. He tried to hold on to the shoes, but they slipped off his feet. They ran away from him, leaving him alone and barefoot. He chased after them, but they were too fast. He saw them disappear into a dark hole. He heard them laugh and say, "Bye bye, Tommy. Have fun with no shoes."
Tommy woke up with a start. He was sweating and shaking. He looked at his feet and saw his old shoes. He felt a pang of guilt and sadness. He realized that he had been very selfish and ungrateful. He wished he could say sorry to his mommy and his friends. He wished he could be a better boy.
He got out of his bed and went to his mommy's room. He knocked on the door and said, "Mommy, I had a bad dream. Can I talk to you?"
His mommy opened the door and hugged him. She said, "Of course, Tommy. What's wrong?"
Tommy told her about his dream and how he felt. He said, "Mommy, I'm sorry for being selfish. I don't need those shoes. I have enough shoes. I have enough everything. I love you, mommy. Can you forgive me?"
His mommy smiled and kissed him. She said, "I love you too, Tommy. And I forgive you. You are not a bad boy. You are a good boy who made a mistake. Everyone makes mistakes. The important thing is to learn from them and to be kind and generous. Do you understand?"
Tommy nodded and hugged his mommy. He said, "I understand, mommy. Thank you for teaching me. Can we go and play with my friends tomorrow? I want to share my toys and my snacks with them. I want to be a good friend."
His mommy said, "That sounds like a wonderful idea, Tommy. I'm proud of you. Now, let's go back to bed and have a good night's sleep. Maybe you'll have a nice dream this time."
Tommy smiled and said, "Maybe I will, mommy. Maybe I will."

"Can I try your soup?" Mia asked Ben. She wanted to taste the red soup.
"OK, but only a little bit," Ben said. He liked his soup a lot and did not want to share too much. He lent his spoon to Mia.
Mia took a sip of the tomato soup. She made a face. She did not like it at all. It was too sour and spicy for her. She gave the spoon back to Ben.
"Yuck, I don't like your soup," Mia said. She was glad she had her own soup.
Ben took his spoon and stirred his soup. He saw something in it that made him miserable. It was a green bean. He hated green beans. They were yucky and crunchy and made him gag.
"Yuck, I don't like my soup," Ben said. He pushed his bowl away.
Mia looked at Ben's soup. She saw the green bean and smiled. She liked green beans. They were yummy and healthy and made her strong.
"Can I have your green bean?" Mia asked Ben.
"OK, but only if you give me something from your soup," Ben said. He wanted to trade the green bean for something he liked.
Mia looked at her soup. She saw a piece of carrot. She liked carrots, but she liked green beans more. She agreed to the trade.
"OK, here is a carrot. Give me the green bean," Mia said. She lent her spoon to Ben.
Ben took the spoon and scooped up the carrot. He gave the spoon and the green bean to Mia.
"Thank you," Mia said. She ate the green bean and smiled.
"You're welcome," Ben said. He ate the carrot and smiled.
They both liked their soup better now. They finished their bowls and asked for more. They were happy and full. They did not need to lend their spoons anymore.

The next day, Tom heard a loud bang from his closet. He ran to see what it was. He opened the closet door and saw the green car on the floor. It was smoking and sparking. The strange symbol on the front was glowing. Tom was scared. He did not know what the car was or what it could do. He wished he had never touched it.
He ran to his mom and told her what happened. She came to his room and saw the green car. She gasped and picked it up. She looked at the symbol and recognized it. It was the logo of an unknown company that made dangerous toys. She had seen it on the news. She told Tom that the car was not a toy, but a bomb. She said he was lucky that it did not explode. She said they had to call the police and get rid of the car.
Tom was shocked and sorry. He did not mean to cause trouble. He said he was sorry and hugged his mom. He said he did not want the green car anymore. He said he only wanted his red car. His mom said it was okay and hugged him back. She said she was proud of him for telling her the truth. She said she loved him and his red car. She said they would never play with unknown toys again.

Sam was angry. He said, "But I want to record the train. It is my turn to play with the machine. You can play with the train later. Let me do it."
Lily was sad. She said, "No, Sam. It is not fair. You always get to do what you want. You never let me choose. I want to play with the train now."
They started to argue. They pulled the train and the machine. They made a big mess. The track broke. The machine stopped. The train fell.
They both cried. They were sorry. They said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry, Lily. I was mean. I was selfish. Can we be friends again?"
They hugged. They fixed the track. They put the train back. They shared the machine. They recorded the train. They listened to it. They laughed. They played. They were happy.

"Wait, Tim!" Mia says. "Ask the owner first!"

Lily and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll and Tom had a car. They were having fun until Tom wanted to play with the doll too.
"Can I have the doll, please?" Tom asked Lily.
"No, it's mine!" Lily said. She hugged the doll and turned away from Tom.
Tom felt sad and angry. He grabbed the car and threw it at Lily. The car hit the doll and made it fall on the floor.
"Hey, that's not nice!" Lily shouted. She picked up the doll and saw that it had a tear on its dress. She started to cry.
Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily crying and Tom looking guilty.
"What happened here?" Mom asked.
Tom sighed. He knew he had done something bad. He wanted to say sorry, but he was afraid that Lily would not forgive him.
Mom looked at Tom and said, "Tell me the truth, Tom. Did you throw the car at Lily?"
Tom nodded. He felt ashamed.
"Why did you do that, Tom?" Mom asked.
"Because I wanted the doll, but Lily wouldn't share," Tom said.
Mom said, "I understand that you wanted the doll, but that's not a good reason to hurt Lily. You should be kind to your sister and respect her things. How would you feel if she threw your car and broke it?"
Tom thought for a moment. He realized that he would feel very sad and angry too.
"I would feel bad, Mom," Tom said.
Mom said, "Then you should say sorry to Lily and help her fix the doll. Maybe she will let you play with it later, if you ask nicely."
Tom looked at Lily, who was still crying. He felt sorry for her and for what he had done.
He walked over to her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong to throw the car at you and your doll. Can I help you fix it?"
Lily looked at Tom and saw that he was sincere. She stopped crying and said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. Thank you for helping me."
They hugged and smiled. Mom was proud of them. She said, "That's very good, Tom and Lily. You are both kind and honest. I love you both very much."
They said, "We love you too, Mom."
They fixed the doll together and then played with both the doll and the car. They shared and had fun. They learned their lesson and were happy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big castle with a king and a queen and some knights and horses. They liked to make up stories about the castle and the people who lived there.
One day, their mom said they had to go to the store with her. She said they could bring one toy each, but they had to be careful not to lose them or spoil them. Lily and Ben both wanted to bring the king, because he was the most important and the most shiny. They argued and fought over the king, and pulled him from each other.
"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. "You are going to break the king, and then you will have no king at all. Why don't you share him, and take turns holding him?"
Lily and Ben did not want to share. They both thought they deserved the king more than the other. They kept on fighting and pulling, until they heard a loud snap. The king's head came off, and rolled under the couch. Lily and Ben gasped, and looked at the broken king in horror.
They both started to cry, and said they were sorry. They wished they had listened to their mom, and shared the king. They tried to put the head back on, but it was too late. The king was spoiled, and could not be fixed.
Their mom came back from the kitchen, and saw what had happened. She was not angry, but she was sad. She hugged Lily and Ben, and said they had learned a hard lesson. She said they still had the queen and the knights and the horses, and they could still play with the castle. She said maybe they could find a new king someday, or make one out of clay or paper.
Lily and Ben nodded, and wiped their tears. They said they would be more careful with their toys, and more kind to each other. They said they would share the queen, and take turns holding her. They said they still loved the castle, and each other.
They went to the store with their mom, and held the queen in their hands. She was not as shiny as the king, but she was mild and sweet. She smiled at Lily and Ben, and they smiled back. They hoped the king was happy under the couch, and they thanked him for his stories.

The squirrel looked at her for a moment, then it let Sarah pet it. As Sarah petted it, the squirrel dropped the necklace into her hand. Sarah was so happy! She cheered and hugged the cute thief, thankful to have her necklace back.

What he saw was a big truck with a lot of men and machines. They were all standing near the river. The leopard was confused, he had never seen something like this before. He watched them for a while and realized they were building something. He was curious, so he decided to get closer and see what was going on. He was excited to learn something new! When he got there he found out that the men were building a new bridge. The leopard was so happy. Now he could cross the river without getting wet! The new bridge was a great addition to his home and everyone around was very happy too.

The sun was shining brightly as Chester wandered through the woods. Birds were chirping and swing from tree to tree. He happily followed the riverside, hopping from rock to rock. Suddenly, he heard a voice coming from the pond.
"Hello, sweet Chester," it said.
Chester looked around, but he couldn't see anyone.
"Who are you?" he asked.
"I'm the frog from the pond," answered the voice.
Chester was very surprised. He had never seen a talking frog before!
"What do you want me to do?" he asked the frog.
"Follow the path around the pond," said the Frog. "It will take you to a sweet surprise!"
So Chester followed the path, until he came to a big tree full of ripe apples. He was so excited he almost forgot about the frog.
"Thank you for the sweet surprise," he said as he filled his pockets with apples. "I'll come back and visit you soon!"
And he waved goodbye to the frog before skipping away, back through the woods.

Once upon a time there was a small fat seal who lived by the sea shore. Every day, she would lay in the sun and measure how much time had passed. One day, a huge wave came to the shore and washed her away to a small pond. The seal was now stuck in the pond and her only way out was up a slippery rock.
The seal tried to measure the rock with her eyes, but it was too high. She tried to climb up, but her soft, fat body made it hard. With all her strength, she managed to climb halfway up the rock, but kept slipping back down. The seal began to cry in frustration.
Just then, a small voice said, "I can help you, little seal". The voice belonged to a kind old turtle who was watching from the safety of the pond. He said, "If you measure one small step at a time, you will be able to reach the top."
The seal thought about this advice and tried to take it one small step at a time. She was soon at the top of the rock! She thanked the turtle for his help and waddled back safely to the shore.
The moral of this story is that sometimes tackling something big is easier if we break it down into smaller achievable steps.

Once upon a time, there was a big comet in the sky. Everyone was looking up and pointing and chatting about how beautiful it was. 
One day, a little girl called Bella was playing in the park. Suddenly, she heard a loud ringing sound! It was coming from the comet in the sky.
Bella asked her mom, "Mommy, what's that ringing noise?". Her mom said, "That's the comet ringing."
"But why is it ringing, mommy?" asked Bella. Her mom said, "The comet is ringing because it's getting closer and closer to the Earth and it wants us to listen to it." 
Bella looked at the big comet. She wanted to go up and touch it. But mom said, "No Bella, you can't touch the comet. It's too far away for us."
Bella was disappointed, but she accepted the answer. She waved to the big comet in the sky and it kept ringing for a long time.
