"My name is Lily. This is my pot. I use it to make music." Lily says. She bangs the pot with a spoon. It makes a loud sound.
"Wow, that is a nice pot. Can we play with you?" Ben asks.
"Sure, you can play with me. But you have to share the pot. It is my favorite thing." Lily says.
Sara and Ben are happy. They take turns to bang the pot with the spoon. They make a lot of noise. They laugh and sing.
But Tom is not happy. He is envious. He wants the pot for himself. He thinks it is not fair that Lily has such a big and shiny pot. He waits until Lily is not looking. Then he runs and grabs the pot. He runs away with it.
"Hey, that is my pot! Give it back!" Lily shouts.
"Stop, Tom! That is not nice!" Sara and Ben shout.
They chase after Tom. They catch him and take the pot back. They give it to Lily. They are angry with Tom.
"Tom, you are mean. You cannot take things that are not yours. You have to say sorry to Lily." Sara says.
"Sorry, Lily. I was envious. I wanted your pot. But I know it is wrong. Can you forgive me?" Tom says.
Lily is sad. But she is also kind. She thinks for a moment. Then she says:
"Okay, Tom. I forgive you. But you have to promise to be nice and share. Do you want to play with us?"
Tom nods. He is sorry. He wants to be friends. He says:
"Yes, please. I want to play with you. Thank you, Lily."
Lily smiles. She gives Tom the spoon. She says:
"Here, you can bang the pot with me. But be careful. It is loud."
They all play together. They make music with the pot. They have fun. They are friends.

Ben and Jen are twins. They like to play on the farm with their grandpa. Grandpa has a mule named Max. Max is big and brown and has long ears. He is very slow and likes to eat grass.
One day, Ben and Jen want to help grandpa cut the hay. They ask grandpa if they can ride on Max. Grandpa says yes, but they have to be careful and hold on tight. He gives them a big hat and a small knife each. He tells them to cut the hay that is dry and yellow.
Ben and Jen climb on Max and grandpa leads him to the field. They see the hay that is dry and yellow. They start to cut the hay with their small knives. They put the hay in a big basket that is on Max's back. They are having fun and they sing a song.
But Max is very slow and he does not like to work. He sees some grass that is green and juicy. He stops and starts to eat the grass. Ben and Jen try to make him move, but he does not listen. He eats and eats and eats. He does not care about the hay.
Grandpa sees that Max is not moving. He comes to see what is wrong. He sees that Max is eating the grass and that Ben and Jen are stuck on his back. He laughs and says, "Max, you are a lazy mule! You have to finish your job before you can eat!" He pulls Max by the rope and makes him move. He helps Ben and Jen cut the rest of the hay. He says, "You did a good job, Ben and Jen! You are very helpful and brave!" He gives them a hug and a cookie. Ben and Jen are happy and they say, "Thank you, grandpa! We love you and we love Max!"

A wise old lady saw what happened. She came to Lily and Ben and gave them some cookies. She said, "Don't be mad at each other. It was not your fault. The dog was naughty and greedy. You should be kind and forgiving. Friends are more important than sandwiches."

Anna and Ben love to play with their toy jet. It is red and shiny and makes a loud noise when they push a button. They pretend they are pilots and fly to different places.
One day, they decide to fly to the zoo. They put on their helmets and sunglasses and get in the jet. Anna is the captain and Ben is the co-pilot. They say, "Ready for takeoff!"
They zoom through the air and see many things. They see birds and clouds and houses and cars. They see a big river and a bridge. They see a park and a playground. They have fun and talk to each other.
"Look, Ben, there is the zoo!" Anna says. "I see it, Anna, let's land there!" Ben says. They find a spot to park their jet and get out. They run to the gate and buy tickets.
They see many animals at the zoo. They see lions and tigers and bears. They see monkeys and elephants and giraffes. They see penguins and seals and dolphins. They have more fun and learn new things.
They are hungry and thirsty, so they go to the cafeteria. They see a lady who serves food and drinks. She is very nice and smiles at them. She says, "Hello, little pilots, what would you like to have?"
They look at the menu and see many things. They see sandwiches and burgers and pizza. They see juice and milk and soda. They see cookies and cake and ice cream. They have a hard time choosing.
Anna says, "I want a sandwich and juice, please." Ben says, "I want a burger and milk, please." The lady says, "OK, coming right up!" She makes their orders and gives them to them. She says, "Enjoy your meal and have a nice day!"
They say, "Thank you, lady, you are very kind!" They take their trays and find a table. They eat their food and drink their drinks. They are happy and full.
They say, "That was a good lunch, let's go see more animals!" They get up and throw away their trash. They put on their helmets and sunglasses and run back to their jet. They say, "Ready for takeoff!"
They zoom through the air and see more things. They see a rainbow and a balloon. They see a castle and a ferris wheel. They see an enormous plane and a helicopter. They have more fun and talk to each other.
They fly back home and land in their backyard. They get out of their jet and hug it. They say, "Thank you, jet, you are the best!" They take off their helmets and sunglasses and go inside. They tell their mom and dad about their adventure. They say, "We had a great day, we love our jet!"
The end.

Sara was sick. She had a hot head and a sore throat. Mom put a thermometer in her mouth to see how sick she was. Sara did not like the thermometer. It was hard and cold and made her gag. She wanted to spit it out, but Mom said no.
"Be still, Sara. I need to see your temperature. You might have a fever," Mom said.
Sara tried to be still, but she felt very weak. She wanted to lie down and sleep. She did not want to go to school or play with her toys. She just wanted Mom to hug her and make her feel better.
But then she heard a noise. It was Max, her little brother. He was in her room, playing with her dolls. Sara loved her dolls. They were her best friends. She did not want Max to touch them. He was too rough and messy. He might break them or lose them.
"Max, get out of my room! Those are my dolls!" Sara shouted. She jumped out of bed and ran to her room. She forgot about the thermometer in her mouth. It fell on the floor and broke.
Mom heard the noise and followed Sara. She saw the broken thermometer and the angry children. She was very upset.
"Sara, what have you done? You could have hurt yourself with the glass. And you left your door unlocked. Max could have taken anything from your room. You know you have to lock your door when you are sick," Mom scolded.
Sara felt sorry. She did not mean to break the thermometer or leave her door unlocked. She was just mad at Max. She looked at Mom with big, sad eyes.
"I'm sorry, Mom. I was sick and weak and I wanted my dolls. Max was playing with them and I didn't like it," Sara said.
Mom sighed. She knew Sara was sick and weak and she loved her dolls. She also knew Max was curious and bored and he wanted to play. She hugged both of them and said:
"I'm sorry, too. I know you both feel bad. But you have to be careful and respectful. Sara, you have to keep the thermometer in your mouth and lock your door when you are sick. Max, you have to ask before you play with Sara's dolls and leave them as you found them. Can you do that?"
Sara and Max nodded. They said sorry to each other and hugged. Mom smiled and said:
"Good. Now, let's clean up this mess and get you both some juice. Maybe we can watch a movie together and cuddle on the couch. How does that sound?"
Sara and Max smiled. They liked that idea. They followed Mom to the kitchen and forgot about their troubles. They felt a little better.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. Lily found a big spoon and said, "Look, Tom, I have a magic spoon. It can make anything you want."
Tom smiled and said, "Really? Can it make me a cake?"
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, of course. Just close your eyes and wish hard."
Tom closed his eyes and said, "I wish for a cake. A big, yummy cake with icing and sprinkles."
Lily tapped the spoon on the counter and said, "Abracadabra, cake-a-dabra!"
Tom opened his eyes and looked around. He did not see a cake. He saw a big, furry monster with sharp teeth and claws. It came out of the cupboard and roared at them.
Lily and Tom were scared. They screamed and ran away from the monster. They hid behind the sofa and hugged each other.
"Where did that monster come from?" Tom asked.
"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe the spoon was not magic. Maybe it was bad."
They heard the monster banging on the cupboard door. It wanted to get out and chase them.
"What do we do?" Lily asked.
Tom thought for a moment. He said, "Maybe we can make it go away. Maybe we can use the spoon again and wish it away."
Lily said, "Do you think it will work?"
Tom said, "We can try. Come on, let's be brave."
They crawled out from behind the sofa and grabbed the spoon. They held it together and said, "We wish for the monster to go away. We wish for the monster to go away. Abracadabra, monster-a-dabra!"
They heard a loud poof and saw a cloud of smoke. The monster was gone. The cupboard was empty.
Lily and Tom cheered and hugged each other. They said, "We did it! We made the monster go away!"
They decided to put the spoon back in the drawer and never use it again. They said, "Maybe we don't need a magic spoon. Maybe we have enough magic in ourselves."

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play in the park. They liked to swing on the swings, slide on the slides, and run on the grass. One day, they saw a big hill in the park that looked like a volcano. They wanted to climb it and see what was on top.
"Let's go, Lily!" Tom said. "It will be fun!"
"I don't know, Tom," Lily said. "It looks high and steep. What if we fall?"
"Don't be scared, Lily," Tom said. "We are fast and strong. We can do it!"
Tom and Lily started to climb the hill. They used their hands and feet to hold on to the rocks and dirt. They went higher and higher, until they reached the top. They looked around and saw the whole park and the sky.
"Wow, Tom, this is amazing!" Lily said. "We did it!"
"Yes, we did, Lily!" Tom said. "We are the best!"
They were so happy and proud that they did not notice the smoke and fire coming out of the hill. It was a real volcano, and it was about to erupt!
"Look, Tom, look!" Lily said, pointing at the smoke and fire. "The volcano is angry! It is going to spit lava!"
"Uh-oh, Lily, this is bad!" Tom said. "We have to get down, fast!"
Tom and Lily tried to climb down the hill, but it was too late. The volcano erupted, and lava started to flow down the hill. It was hot and red and scary. Tom and Lily screamed and cried for help.
"Help, help, help!" they shouted.
Luckily, a fireman heard their cries and came to rescue them. He used a ladder and a rope to pull them up and take them to safety. He was brave and kind.
"Are you okay, kids?" he asked.
"Yes, thank you, fireman!" Tom and Lily said.
"You are very lucky," he said. "You should never climb a volcano. It is very dangerous. You could have been hurt or worse."
"We are sorry, fireman," Tom and Lily said. "We did not know it was a volcano. We just wanted to have fun."
"I understand, kids," he said. "But you should always be careful and listen to your parents and teachers. They know what is good and safe for you. And you should always respect nature and its power. It can be beautiful, but also fierce."
"Yes, fireman, we will," Tom and Lily said.
They learned their lesson and never climbed a volcano again. They still played in the park, but they stayed away from the hill. They swung on the swings, slid on the slides, and ran on the grass. They had fun, but they also had wisdom.

Tom smiled and hugged her. "Thank you, Lily. You are the best sister ever. I will share it with you always."

The next day, they came back to the lake. They wanted to play with the shiny stone again. But when Tom reached into his pocket, he gasped. The stone was gone!
"Where is it? Where is it?" he cried. "I lost it! I lost the pretty stone!"
Lily tried to calm him down. "Don't worry, Tom. Maybe it fell out somewhere. Let's look for it. Maybe we can find it."
They searched the shore and the grass and the trees. But they could not find the stone. They felt very sad and sorry.
They did not know that the stone was not really a stone. It was a special egg that belonged to a big turtle. The turtle had left it on the shore to warm up in the sun. But when it came back, it saw that the egg was gone. It was very angry and scared. It followed the scent of the children and found the egg in Tom's pocket. It snatched it away and swam back to the lake. It was very happy and proud.

Tom and Jen were twins who liked to eat out with their mom and dad. They always got to choose what they wanted from the menu, which had pictures of different foods. Tom liked to try new things, like fish or salad or soup. Jen always wanted the same thing: chicken nuggets and fries.
One day, they went to a new restaurant that had a special menu for kids. Tom saw a picture of a pizza with cheese and ham and pineapple. He thought it looked yummy and asked for it. Jen saw a picture of chicken nuggets and fries and asked for it.
The waiter brought their food and they started to eat. Tom liked his pizza very much and said, "This is so good! Do you want to try some, Jen?" Jen looked at his pizza and said, "No, thank you. I only like chicken nuggets and fries." Tom shrugged and ate some more.
Then, he saw something on Jen's plate that he had never seen before. It was a green thing with a stem and a leaf. He asked, "What is that, Jen?" Jen said, "I don't know. It came with my chicken nuggets and fries. I don't want it." Tom said, "Can I have it?" Jen said, "Sure, take it. I don't like green things."
Tom took the green thing and bit into it. It was crunchy and sweet and juicy. He said, "Wow, this is delicious! It's a grape! Do you want to try some, Jen?" Jen looked at his grape and said, "No, thank you. I only like chicken nuggets and fries." Tom shrugged and ate some more.
When they finished their food, the waiter came back and asked, "Did you enjoy your meal, kids?" Tom said, "Yes, thank you. It was very good. I liked the pizza and the grape." Jen said, "Yes, thank you. It was okay. I liked the chicken nuggets and fries." The waiter smiled and said, "I'm glad you liked your food. You know, it's wise to try new things sometimes. You might discover something you love. Like this grape, for example. It's good for you, too. It has vitamins and water and sugar. It's a fruit. Do you know what a fruit is?" Tom said, "Yes, I do. A fruit is a sweet thing that grows on a plant. Like an apple or a banana or a grape." Jen said, "No, I don't. I only know chicken nuggets and fries."
The waiter said, "Well, maybe next time you can try a fruit, Jen. Or something else from the menu. There are many yummy things to eat in the world. You might like them if you give them a chance. Don't resist new things, Jen. Be brave and curious, like your brother Tom." Jen looked at Tom and saw that he was happy and full. She looked at her plate and saw that she had left the grape. She felt a little sad and hungry. She wondered what a fruit tasted like. She wished she had tried the grape.
The moral of the story is: It's good to try new things. You might find something you love and learn something new. Don't resist new things. Be brave and curious.

But Lily's friend begged and begged, and Lily finally gave in. As her friend rode the scooter, Lily felt embarrassed that she had been so selfish. She realized that sharing was more important than keeping her scooter all to herself.
Unfortunately, as her friend was riding the scooter, she lost control and crashed into a tree. The scooter was broken, and Lily was very sad. She wished she had never let her friend ride it. From then on, Lily learned to be more careful with her things and to always think twice before sharing them.

"No, you won't! I have a strong shield! I will protect myself and the castle!" Ben said.

"What is that?" Ben asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a real dragon!" Lily said.

Ben and Lily cried and wished they had a real knight to save them. But no one came. The dog was too strong and mean. It did not let them go. It was a bad ending.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw big clouds in the sky. They heard their mom say, "There is a hurricane coming. We have to go inside and stay safe."
Lily and Ben did not know what a hurricane was. They thought it was a game. They said, "Let's play hurricane! We can run and spin and make noise like the wind!"
They grabbed their coats and hats and ran to the backyard. They pretended to be the wind and the rain. They spun around and shouted, "Hurricane! Hurricane!"
Their mom saw them and called, "Lily! Ben! Come inside now! It's not safe to play outside! The hurricane is real and it's very strong!"
Lily and Ben did not listen. They thought their mom was playing too. They said, "No, mom! We are having fun! We are the hurricane!"
But then, they felt the wind get stronger and colder. They saw the trees sway and the leaves fly. They heard a loud roar in the air. They felt scared and cold.
They realized their mom was right. The hurricane was not a game. It was a big storm that could hurt them. They said, "Mom! Help! We want to go inside!"
Their mom ran to them and hugged them. She said, "It's okay, my loves. I'm here. I will lead you inside. We will be warm and safe together."
She took their hands and led them to the house. They closed the door and the windows. They cuddled on the couch and watched the storm pass. They learned their lesson. They never played hurricane again.

"Come on, Ben, let's go in the pit!" Lila urged. She ran towards the hole.
"No, Lila, stop!" Ben shouted. He was scared of the pit. He thought it was dark and dirty. He did not want to go in the pit.
But Lila did not listen. She jumped into the pit. She landed on something soft and furry. It was a bear. The bear was sleeping in the pit. Lila screamed. The bear woke up. It was angry.
"Roar!" The bear roared. It showed its big teeth and claws. It wanted to eat Lila.
"Help, help!" Lila cried. She was sorry she went into the pit. She wished she listened to Ben.
Ben heard Lila's cry. He was brave. He ran to the pit. He saw the bear. He picked up a stick. He threw the stick at the bear. The stick hit the bear's nose. The bear was hurt. It ran away.
"Come on, Lila, climb up!" Ben said. He reached out his hand. He helped Lila out of the pit. Lila hugged Ben. She was happy he saved her.
"Thank you, Ben, you are my hero!" Lila said.
"You're welcome, Lila, you are my friend!" Ben said.
They ran back to the park. They played on the swings and the slide. They had fun. They never went near the pit again. They learned their lesson. The end.

"Look, look, it's hatching!" Lily said. She and Tom moved closer to the egg and saw a small head poke out. It was a baby bird, but not like any bird they had seen before. It had feathers of many colors, like the egg, and it also glowed.

They smiled and played with the bird. They gave it a name: Sparky. They did not know where it came from or where it would go, but they knew they loved it. And they knew it loved them too.

"It's OK, kids. I'm not angry. I'm glad you found the camera. It's very special to me and my son. You can keep it if you want. But you have to promise me something," the man said.

"No, you can't!" Ben said. "If I give you one block, then I won't have a triangle anymore. I will have a line. I don't want a line. I want a triangle."

"What's wrong, sweeties?" Mom asked.

"Ben, is that true?" Mom asked.

"Yes, I do!" Lila said. "Let's make more shapes together!"

Tim and Mia liked to play on the beach. They liked to make marks in the sand with their fingers and toes. They liked to watch the surf crash on the shore. They liked to find shells and rocks and seaweed.
One day, they found a big shell that was shiny and pink. It had a hole in it, like a door. Mia said, "Look, Tim, a shell house! Maybe a crab lives inside." Tim said, "Let's take it home and put it in our room. It's so pretty and fragile. We have to be careful not to break it."
They wrapped the shell in a towel and put it in their backpack. They ran back to their mom, who was sitting under an umbrella. She said, "Did you have fun, kids? What did you find?" Tim and Mia showed her the shell. She said, "Wow, that's a beautiful shell. Where did you find it?" They told her they found it near the surf. She said, "That's lucky. But you know, sometimes the surf can bring surprises. You never know what might come out of the water."
They didn't understand what she meant. They thought she was just joking. They went home and put the shell on their dresser. They admired it and imagined what kind of crab lived inside. They went to bed and dreamed of the beach.

And in the middle of the mess, there was a big, green, slimy octopus. It had eight long arms and two big eyes. It looked angry and scared. It had crawled out of the shell in the night and tried to escape.
Tim and Mia screamed. Their mom came running. She saw the octopus and said, "Oh, no! How did that get here? That's not a crab, that's an octopus! It must have been hiding in the shell. The surf must have washed it up on the beach. Poor thing, it needs water. We have to take it back to the sea."
She grabbed a bucket and filled it with water. She carefully picked up the octopus and put it in the bucket. She told Tim and Mia to get dressed and follow her. Mom came to his room and saw him on his bed. She felt his forehead and said, "Oh, Tom, you have a fever. You ate too much candy. That was not a good idea. Candy is not good for you if you eat too much. You need to eat your dinner first."
Tom said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I was wrong. I should have eaten my dinner. I should have tried the green things. Maybe they are not so sour. Can I have some dinner now?"
Mom said, "Yes, you can have some dinner now. But you have to drink some water first. And you have to rest for a while. Then you can have some dinner. And maybe a little candy. But only a little."
Tom said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you. I will eat my dinner and listen to you next time."
Mom said, "I love you too, Tom. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Dinner is important. And so is being polite and trying new things. Sometimes, they are not so bad as you think."
The end.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play chess. Chess is a game with black and white pieces. You move the pieces on a board with squares. You try to catch the king of the other color.
One day, Tom and Sam go to the park. They bring their chess board and pieces. They find a nice spot under a big tree. The tree gives them shade. Shade is good when the sun is very bright and hot.
They start to play chess. Tom is white and Sam is black. Tom moves his pieces fast. He wants to win. Sam moves his pieces slow. He thinks a lot. He wants to win too.
"Check!" Tom says. He moves his queen next to Sam's king. He smiles. He thinks he will win soon.
"Check!" Sam says. He moves his knight next to Tom's king. He smiles too. He has a surprise for Tom.
Tom looks at the board. He sees Sam's knight. He sees his king. He sees no way to save his king. He is sad. He says, "Oh no! You win!"
Sam says, "Yes! I win! I have a name for this move. It is called 'fork'. Do you know why?"
Tom says, "No. Why?"
Sam says, "Because my knight forks your king and your queen. It attacks both of them at the same time. You have to move your king, but then I can take your queen. And then you have no chance."
Tom says, "Wow. That is a clever move. I did not see it. You are good at chess."
Sam says, "Thank you. You are good too. But you have to be careful. Sometimes the board can change in one move. You have to look at all the pieces and all the squares. Chess is a fun game, but it is also a hard game."
Tom says, "You are right. Chess is fun and hard. I want to play again. Can we play again?"
Sam says, "Sure. We can play again. But let's switch colors. You can be black and I can be white. Maybe that will make a difference."
Tom says, "OK. Let's switch. Maybe I can win this time."
They switch colors. They set up the board. They start to play again. They are happy. They like to play chess. Chess is their favorite game.

The owner of the cake says, "Thank you. And don't worry. The cake was not very good anyway. It had a funny taste."

The truck man looks at them. He smiles. He says, "Sure, kids. What do you have in your bag?"
Lily and Ben show him their things. The truck man likes the cookies and the ball. He says, "OK, I will trade you these for some pebbles. But not too many. I need them for my work."
He gives them a small bucket. He lets them fill it with pebbles. Lily and Ben are happy. They say, "Thank you, truck man!"
They take their bucket and run to their yard. They dump the pebbles on the grass. They start to play with them. They make shapes and patterns. They have fun.
But they also make a mess. The pebbles are everywhere. Some are on the sidewalk. Some are in the flower bed. Some are in the dog's bowl.
Mom sees the mess. She is not happy. She says, "Lily and Ben, what have you done? You have made a mess with the pebbles. Where did you get them?"
Lily and Ben tell her the story. They say, "We bought them from the truck man. We traded with him. He was nice."
Mom shakes her head. She says, "You should not trade with strangers, kids. And you should not make a mess with the pebbles. They are not toys. They are for building roads and houses. You have to clean them up. Now."
Lily and Ben are sad. They say, "Sorry, Mom."
They start to pick up the pebbles. They put them back in the bucket. They are careful not to lose any. They say, "We will not buy pebbles again. We will play with something else."
Mom hugs them. She says, "I love you, kids. But please be more careful next time. And ask me before you trade with anyone."
Lily and Ben nod. They say, "We love you, Mom. And we will."

Lily ran to the kitchen and saw that there was a leak under the sink. Her mom was trying to fix it, but the water kept coming out.
"I need you to be patient, Lily. This might take a while," her mom said.
Lily watched as her mom worked on the leak. After a few minutes, Lily's dad came into the kitchen.
"I can help with that," he said.
"No, I insist. I can do it myself," her mom replied.
Lily watched as her parents worked together to fix the leak. Finally, after a lot of hard work, the leak was fixed.
"Great job, Mom and Dad!" Lily said, clapping her hands.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. It was dark outside, and she was walking home with her mommy. They had to cross a big street with lots of cars, called traffic. 
Lily was scared of the traffic because it was loud and fast. She held her mommy's hand tightly and didn't want to let go. Suddenly, a car honked really loud and Lily jumped. 
Her mommy saw that she was scared and asked her if she wanted to go back home. Lily shook her head and said no. She wanted to be brave and cross the street. So, she took a deep breath, nodded her head, and they crossed the street safely. 
Afterwards, Lily felt proud of herself for being brave. She smiled and hugged her mommy tightly. They continued walking home, happy and safe.

"What happened?" asked Benny.
"I fell from my nest," said the bird. "I need to find a twig to fix it."
Benny wanted to help. He looked around and found a twig. As he picked it up, he accidentally tore a leaf. 
"Oh no!" said Benny. "I'm sorry, little leaf."
"It's okay," said the bird. "Thank you for the twig."
Benny felt happy he could help, even if he tore a leaf. The sun came out, and the forest was no longer gloomy. Benny and the bird played together all day long.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big billboard with a picture of a clown and some balloons. The billboard said: "Come to the circus! Fun for everyone!"
"Wow, look at that!" Ben said. "I want to go to the circus!"
"Me too!" Anna said. "Maybe we can ask our moms to take us."
They ran to their moms, who were sitting on a bench nearby. They asked them if they could go to the circus.
"Sorry, kids, not today," Anna's mom said. "The circus is too far and too expensive. Maybe another time."
"But we really want to go!" Ben said. "Please, please, please!"
"No, Ben, stop begging," Ben's mom said. "You have to be grateful for what you have. There are many other things you can do for fun."
Anna and Ben felt sad and angry. They walked away from their moms and sat on the grass. They looked at the billboard again and felt jealous of the people who could go to the circus.
"Look at that stupid clown," Ben said. "He thinks he's so funny. I bet he's not even funny at all. He's just silly and ugly."
"Yeah, and look at those balloons," Anna said. "They're so boring and plain. I bet they pop easily and make a loud noise."
They started to tease the billboard and make fun of it. They laughed and pointed at it. They did not notice that a man was watching them from behind a tree. The man was the clown from the billboard. He was on his way to the circus and he heard what Anna and Ben said.
The clown felt hurt and angry. He decided to teach them a lesson. He sneaked up behind them and grabbed their hats. He put them on his head and ran away.
"Hey, give us back our hats!" Anna and Ben shouted. They chased after the clown, but he was too fast and too clever. He dodged and ducked and hid behind cars and trees. He blew his horn and waved his balloons. He made funny faces and noises. He teased Anna and Ben and made fun of them.
Anna and Ben felt scared and embarrassed. They did not like being teased and made fun of. They realized that they had been mean and rude to the clown and the billboard. They felt sorry and ashamed.
"Please, stop teasing us!" Anna said. "We're sorry we teased you and the billboard. We were wrong and mean. Please give us back our hats!"
"Yeah, please, we're sorry!" Ben said. "We won't tease anyone again. We learned our lesson. Please be nice to us!"
The clown stopped and looked at them. He saw that they were sincere and regretful. He felt sorry for them too. He smiled and gave them back their hats.
"Here you go, kids," he said. "I'm sorry I teased you too. I was just trying to show you how it feels. Teasing is not nice and not funny. It hurts people's feelings and makes them sad. You should be kind and respectful to everyone, even if they are different from you. That's the moral of the story."
Anna and Ben nodded and thanked the clown. They apologized again and hugged him. They told him that he was funny and nice and that they liked his balloons. The clown hugged them back and told them that he liked their hats. He invited them to come to the circus with him. He said he had some free tickets and that he would show them around.
Anna and Ben were happy and excited. They ran to their moms and told them what happened. Their moms were surprised and glad. They agreed to let them go to the circus with the clown. They thanked him for his kindness and generosity.
Anna and Ben had a wonderful time at the circus. They saw many amazing and fun things. They laughed and clapped and cheered. They learned to appreciate and enjoy the diversity and beauty of life. They never teased anyone again. They became good friends with the clown and the billboard. They lived happily ever after. The end.

Tom came out from behind the tree and smiled. He said, "You are very quick, Sara. You are a good seeker." Sara said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good hider. Do you want to play again?" Tom nodded and said, "Yes, let's play again. But this time, you hide and I seek."
Sara ran to find a good hiding spot. She saw a big slide and climbed to the top. She hid behind the slide and waited for Tom. She heard Tom counting to ten and then looking for her. She peeked from behind the slide and saw Tom walking around the park. He did not see her. She giggled and said to herself, "I am a better hider than Tom."
Tom looked for Sara for a long time. He checked behind the trees, under the benches, and in the bushes. He could not find Sara. He started to feel dizzy from running around so much. He said to himself, "Where is Sara? She is a very good hider. Maybe she is hiding in the sky or under the ground."
Sara saw Tom looking tired and dizzy. She felt sorry for him. She decided to give him a hint. She shouted from the top of the slide, "Tom, Tom, look up, look up!" Tom heard Sara's voice and looked up. He saw her waving from the slide. He smiled and said, "I found you, Sara!"
Sara slid down the slide and ran to Tom. She said, "You are a good seeker, Tom. But I am a better hider. Do you surrender?" Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I surrender. You win, Sara. You are the best at hide and seek." Sara hugged Tom and said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. Do you want to play something else?" Tom nodded and said, "Yes, let's play something else. How about tag?" Sara said, "OK, let's play tag. But you have to catch me first." She ran away from Tom and said, "Tag, you're it!" Tom laughed and chased after Sara. They played tag until it was time to go home. They had a lot of fun in the park.

Lily was a little girl who liked to learn new things. She wanted to be independent and do things by herself. One day, she asked her mom if she could teach her how to swim in the water.
"Sure, Lily, I can teach you how to swim. But you have to listen to me and be careful, okay?" her mom said.
"Okay, mom, I will listen and be careful. I want to swim like a fish!" Lily said.
They went to the pool and put on their swimsuits. Lily's mom held her hand and walked with her into the water. The water was cold and wet, but Lily was not afraid. She smiled and splashed with her mom.
"First, you have to learn how to float. Float means to stay on top of the water and not sink. Can you do that?" her mom asked.
"I can try, mom. How do I float?" Lily asked.
"You have to relax your body and breathe slowly. Look at the sky and let the water hold you. I will help you, don't worry," her mom said.
Lily's mom gently lifted her up and placed her on the water. Lily felt the water under her back and around her arms and legs. She looked at the sky and saw the sun and the clouds. She breathed slowly and relaxed her body. She felt the water hold her and she smiled.
"I'm floating, mom, I'm floating!" Lily said.
"Good job, Lily, you're floating! You're learning how to swim!" her mom said.
Lily was happy and proud. She wanted to learn more and be more independent. She thanked her mom for teaching her how to float and asked her what was next.
"Next, we can learn how to kick and move in the water. Do you want to try that?" her mom asked.
"Yes, mom, I want to try that. I want to swim like a fish!" Lily said.
They continued to practice and have fun in the water. Lily learned how to kick and move and swim with her mom. She was independent and brave and curious. She loved the water and her mom. She had a great day.

Sara has an idea. She says, "Ben, let's tear the toast. Maybe we can find butter and jam inside."
Ben thinks that is a good idea. He says, "OK, Sara. Let's tear the toast."
They start to tear the toast. They tear it into small pieces. They tear it into crumbs. They do not find any butter and jam. They only make a big mess.
They hear a knock on the door. It is Grandma. She comes to watch them while Mom is at work. She sees the toast crumbs on the table and on the floor. She sees Sara and Ben with tears in their eyes.
She says, "Oh, my! What happened here? Why did you tear the toast?"
Sara and Ben tell her what happened. They tell her that Mom forgot to put butter and jam on the toast. They tell her that they tried to find butter and jam inside the toast. They tell her that they are sorry for making a mess.
Grandma smiles. She says, "I understand, kids. You were disappointed and curious. But you should not tear the toast. That is wasteful and rude. You should eat what Mom gives you. She works hard to make you breakfast. She loves you very much."
Sara and Ben feel ashamed. They say, "We are sorry, Grandma. We love Mom too. We will not tear the toast again."
Grandma says, "That's good, kids. I forgive you. And I have a surprise for you. I brought some butter and jam with me. How about we make some new toast and put butter and jam on it? Would you like that?"
Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, please, Grandma. Thank you, Grandma. You are very kind."
Grandma hugs them. She says, "You are welcome, kids. You are very kind too. Now, let's clean up this mess and make some yummy toast."

"OK, lady," Anna says. "Thank you. We will try."
The lady leaves. Ben and Anna set up the board. They switch the pieces. They play again. They are lively and happy. They talk and laugh. They do not fight. They do not cheat. They do not lie. They play fair. They have fun. They are friends.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big hill with many small holes. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Look, ants!" Tom said, pointing at the holes. "They are so tiny and busy. Can we meet them?"
"OK, but be careful. Don't hurt them or make them angry," Mom said.
Tom and Lily knelt down and watched the ants. They saw them carry bits of leaves and crumbs to their holes. They saw them talk to each other with their feelers. They saw them work together as a team.
"Hello, ants!" Lily said softly. "We are Tom and Lily. We are your friends. Can we play with you?"
Some ants stopped and looked at Lily. They did not understand her words, but they sensed her kindness. They waved their feelers back at her.
"Hi, friends!" one ant said in ant language. "We are the red ants. We live in this hill. We are happy to meet you."
But not all ants were friendly. Some ants were greedy and mean. They did not like Tom and Lily. They wanted to keep all the food for themselves. They saw Tom holding a cookie in his hand. They wanted to take it from him.
"Look, food!" one greedy ant said in ant language. "That big thing has a delicious cookie. Let's get it!"
The greedy ants ran towards Tom. They climbed on his hand and bit his fingers. They tried to pull the cookie away from him.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "The ants are biting me! They are taking my cookie! Help!"
Mom heard Tom's cry. She ran to him and brushed off the ants. She checked his hand and saw some red marks.
"Are you OK, Tom?" Mom asked. "Did the ants hurt you?"
"Yes, Mom. They hurt me. They are bad ants. They are not our friends," Tom said, sobbing.
Mom hugged Tom and gave him a band-aid. She explained to him that not all ants were bad, but some were greedy and mean. She told him to be careful and respectful of the ants, and to share his food with them if he wanted to.
"OK, Mom. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to make them angry. I will share my cookie with them," Tom said.
He broke his cookie in half and gave one piece to Lily. He put the other piece near the ant hill. He hoped the ants would like it.
The red ants saw the cookie piece. They smelled its sweetness. They thanked Tom and Lily in ant language. They shared the cookie with their friends. They thought Tom and Lily were good and generous. They wanted to be their friends.
"Thank you, friends!" one red ant said in ant language. "You are very kind. You gave us a delicious cookie. We are happy to meet you."
Tom and Lily smiled. They felt happy too. They had met the ants. They had learned something new. They had made some friends.

"It's okay, Sara," her mom said. "I'm glad you are not badly hurt. But you have to learn to be careful and obey when I tell you something. Curiosity is good, but safety is important too. Next time, ask me before you touch something you don't know."
Sara nodded and hugged her mom. She learned her lesson and decided to be more careful and respectful. She also realized that shrimp were not her favorite food. She preferred apples and cheese.

One day, a fisherman went to the lake with his boat. He wanted to catch some fish for his dinner. He had a rod, a hook and a worm. He put the worm on the hook and threw it into the water.
Soon, he felt a tug on his rod. He pulled it up and saw a big green fish. He was very happy and said, "Wow, what a nice fish! I will take you home and cook you." But the fish did not want to go with the fisherman. It said, "Please, let me go. I have a family in the lake. They will miss me."
The fisherman was surprised. He did not know that fish could talk. He felt sorry for the fish and said, "OK, I will let you go. But you have to promise me something. You have to pick a friend for me from the lake. A friend who does not talk and does not have a family. A friend who will be tasty and make me full."
The fish agreed. It said, "Thank you, fisherman. You are very kind. I will pick a friend for you. Wait here." The fish swam away and looked for a friend for the fisherman. It saw many fish, but they all had families or could talk. It did not want to pick them.
Then, it saw a green frog. The frog was sitting on a lily pad. It did not have a family or talk. It only croaked. The fish thought, "This is a good friend for the fisherman. He will not miss it." The fish swam to the frog and said, "Hello, frog. Do you want to play with me?" The frog said, "Sure, fish. What do you want to play?" The fish said, "Let's play catch. I will throw you to the fisherman. He will catch you and be happy." The frog said, "OK, fish. That sounds fun." The fish took the frog in its mouth and threw it to the fisherman.
The fisherman saw the frog flying in the air. He caught it with his hand and said, "Thank you, fish. You picked a good friend for me. This frog will be delicious and make me full." He put the frog in his boat and waved to the fish. The fish waved back and said, "You're welcome, fisherman. Goodbye and good luck." The fisherman rowed his boat back to the shore. He cooked the frog and ate it. He was very happy. The fish swam back to its family. It was very happy too. The end.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they decided to have a picnic in the park. They packed some bread, cheese, apples and juice in a basket and walked to the park.
The park was very big and green, with many flowers and trees. The sun was bright and warm, and the sky was blue. Anna and Ben found a nice spot under a big tree and spread a blanket on the grass. They opened their basket and started to eat their picnic.
"Yum, this cheese is good!" said Anna.
"I like the apples, they are sweet and crunchy!" said Ben.
They ate and drank and talked and laughed. They were very happy.
After they finished their picnic, they decided to play a game. They took turns to say "freeze" and the other one had to stop moving and stay still like a statue. It was a fun game and they made funny poses and faces.
"Freeze!" said Anna, and Ben stopped with his arms in the air and his tongue out.
"Freeze!" said Ben, and Anna stopped with her legs crossed and her eyes closed.
They giggled and tried to make each other laugh.
But then, they heard a loud noise. It was a big dog, barking and running towards them. The dog looked angry and scary. Anna and Ben were afraid. They wanted to run away, but they remembered their game. They were frozen!
"What do we do?" whispered Anna.
"I don't know!" whispered Ben.
The dog came closer and closer. It sniffed their basket and their blanket. It growled and showed its teeth. Anna and Ben were very scared. They wished they could move.
But then, they heard another noise. It was a man, calling the dog. He was the dog's owner. He came to the park and saw the dog and the children.
"Rex, come here!" he shouted. "Bad dog, leave them alone!"
He ran to the dog and grabbed its collar. He pulled the dog away from Anna and Ben. He looked at the children and said, "I'm sorry, are you okay? My dog is not very friendly, he doesn't like strangers. He escaped from the yard and I was looking for him. He didn't hurt you, did he?"
Anna and Ben shook their heads. They were still frozen, but they were relieved. The man was nice and he saved them.
"Thank you, mister," said Anna.
"Yes, thank you," said Ben.
The man smiled and said, "You're welcome. You're very brave, you didn't scream or cry. But you know, you don't have to play freeze when there is danger. You can run or call for help. That's safer and smarter."
Anna and Ben nodded. They understood. They learned a lesson. They said goodbye to the man and the dog and packed their basket and blanket. They walked back home, holding hands.
They still liked to play freeze, but only when it was safe and fun. They never played freeze when there was danger. They knew when to move and when to stay still. They were good friends and good children.

Anna wanted a puppy for her birthday. She asked her mom and dad many times, but they always said no. They said puppies were too much work and too messy. Anna was sad. She loved puppies and wanted to play with one.
On her birthday, Anna woke up and saw a big box with a bow in the living room. She ran to it and opened it. Inside was a stuffed puppy. It was soft and brown and had a red collar. Anna smiled. It was not a real puppy, but it was still cute. She hugged it and named it Spot.

"Thank you, mom and dad. I like it very much," Anna said. She was happy, but she still wished she had a real puppy.
She took Spot to her room and played with him. She pretended he was alive and talked to him. She fed him, brushed him, and took him for walks. She had fun, but she also felt lonely. She wanted a friend who could talk back and play with her.
One day, she saw a sign in the park. It said, "Free puppies. Need good homes." Anna's eyes lit up. She ran to the sign and saw a lady with a basket of puppies. They were all different colors and sizes. They were wagging their tails and barking.
"Can I have one, please?" Anna asked the lady.
"Sure, sweetie. You can pick one. They are all very friendly and healthy," the lady said.
Anna looked at the puppies. They were all so cute. She wanted to take them all home. But she knew she could only have one. She saw a small black puppy with white spots. He looked at her with big brown eyes. He seemed perfect. Anna reached for him.
"Wait a minute, Anna," a voice said. It was her mom. She had followed Anna to the park. "You can't have a puppy. You know that. We already talked about it."
"But mom, please. Look at him. He's perfect. He needs a home. And I need a friend," Anna said. She held the puppy close to her chest. He licked her face.
"Anna, I'm sorry, but no. Puppies are not toys. They are living beings. They need a lot of care and attention. They need food, water, shelter, vet visits, training, and love. They also make noise, mess, and trouble. You are not ready for that. You have Spot. He's your friend. He doesn't need anything. He's perfect for you," her mom said.
Anna looked at her mom. She looked at the puppy. She felt torn. She loved the puppy, but she also loved her mom. She knew her mom was right. Puppies were not easy. She remembered how Spot never cried, bit, or pooped. He was always there for her. He was perfect for her.
She sighed. She kissed the puppy and gave him back to the lady. "I'm sorry, little guy. I can't take you. But I hope you find a good home. You are perfect, too," she said.
She took Spot from her mom and hugged him. "Come on, Spot. Let's go home. You are my friend. You are perfect for me," she said.
Her mom smiled and hugged her. "You are a good girl, Anna. You made a hard choice, but a wise one. I'm proud of you. You are perfect for me, too," she said.
They walked home together, happy and content. Anna learned that sometimes you have to say no to what you want, and yes to what you need. She learned that perfect is not always what it seems. She learned that love is more than just a feeling. It is also a decision. And she decided to love Spot, her perfect friend.

Suddenly, he heard a friendly meow behind him. He jumped round and saw a cat. The cat said "Don't worry little doggy, I know a way out of the forest. Follow me!" West and the cat ran out of the dark forest and back to the park. West was so happy and never strayed too far away again!

Once upon a time there lived a kind woodpecker. He was looking for a place to belong. He wanted to make a home for himself so he searched and searched through the wood. Soon he found a big old tree and he thumped on the tree trunk. It sounded so strong it gave him a feeling of belonging. He decided to make it his home.
He tapped and chipped and drilled until there were two big holes on the trunk. He inspected it carefully and it was perfect. He went into the treehouse and tucked himself in. It was the perfect place to belong.
The woodpecker took extra care to make sure he was kind to all his new friends in the wood. He shared his food and always said please and thank you. All the birds in the wood were so happy to have him there that they invited the woodpecker to the bird ball in the forest. He had a wonderful time and he felt so happy to belong.
He loved his new home and he was so very kind. The wood had made him find his true place to belong.

Once upon a time, there was a happy seal. He lived in a far away ocean, far away from humans.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved the beach. Every day, she would go and stroll along the shore and look at the beautiful shells she would find.
One day she noticed a perfect white shell and ran over to pick it up. She grinned with delight as she held it in her hands. It was so perfect!
When she was just about to put the shell in her pocket, she heard a voice coming from the shell! Startled, she dropped it back on the sand and stepped away.
The voice called out again - this time it said, "Come with me!"
The little girl wasn't sure what to do. She didn't know what was inside the shell. After taking a deep breath, she decided to come, so she bent down and carefully picked up the shell.
She opened it and inside were two little creatures made entirely of sand. They smiled up at her, "Please come with us on an adventure!"
The little girl had never been on an adventure before, but she knew it sounded like fun. Taking the shell in her hand, she smiled and said, "Let's go!"
And so the little girl, together with the two little creatures inside the perfect shell, went on a grand and wonderful adventure!

The children who went to the school loved it. Every morning they would swing open the shiny doors and walk up the polished corridors to their classrooms. At the end of the day, they would run down the sparkling streets and go home with a smile on their face.
Paul worked hard to make sure that the nice school looked its best. All his polishing kept it looking and smelling wonderful. 
The end.

One day a little girl wanted to understand numbers, so she asked her mom. Her mom smiled and said "Ok, let me show you". She pointed to one of the walls and said, "that is one". The girl nodded, she had understood. Then her mom said "now look, here is two". The girl nodded again. They went through numbers 1 to 10 this way and the girl was happy. 
Suddenly, her mom became angry, she saw that a silly bird had made a mess on the table. She said "Oh no, we must clean this up now!" But the girl said, "No, I want to keep learning!" Her mom shook her head in disbelief, she thought the girl was being foolish. But the girl was determined and she nodded again. 
The mom smiled at her, trying again to teach her the numbers. They went past 10 and the girl was now able to count up to 20! She was so happy, she jumped up and down in excitement. The mom laughed and said, "See, you can do it! Now, let's go and clean up that silly bird's mess!"

Andy was so excited! He said, "Yay! I can't wait!"

Once upon a time, there was a big, heavy dinosaur. He walked around and ate plants all day. Then one day, he saw something that made him very angry. It was a tiny little bug! The dinosaur opened his big mouth and tried to bite the bug. But the bug was too fast and flew away. 
The dinosaur was still angry and he started to stomp around. Suddenly, he heard something behind him. He turned around and saw another big, heavy dinosaur. This dinosaur was even bigger than him! He opened his mouth wide and bit down on the other dinosaur. But it was too late - the other dinosaur bit him right back. 
The two dinosaurs kept biting each other until they both got really tired. So they stopped and just lay in the sun. They were both very hungry, but they had no more energy to look for food. So they just fell asleep in the warm sunshine.

But then the little girl got too close and before she knew it, she fell! Down, down, down she went, all the way to the planet. When she landed, the planet was deafeningly quiet! The little girl was very scared, but then she looked up and saw a furry creature staring down at her. 
The creature smiled and waved. The little girl smiled back and waved too. After a few minutes, the creature flew up to the sky, and the little girl followed. Together, they flew all the way back to the little girl's home.
The little girl was very happy and thanked the creature for taking her on the special adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a very icy statue. It was standing in the middle of a cold field and no one could touch it. For days, animals and people passed by, but no one knew it's name.
One day, a young boy stopped by the statue. His name was Jimmy and he was only three years old. He had heard the stories about the icy statue and he wanted find out it's name. So Jimmy stepped closer and he stuck out his hand. His little fingers froze as they touched the icy cold statue, but Jimmy did not stop. 
He said, "what's your name?".
All of the sudden the icy statue started glowing brightly. The whole field lit up. Then the statue spoke, "My name is Frosty". Then, it burst into hundreds of little sparkling diamonds that flew away into the sky.
Since then, every time Jimmy walked through the cold field he thought of Frosty the icy statue and smiled.

The mom and the girl left the toy store without the doll. They walked around the mall and saw a man who didn't know much about the mall. He was lost. The mom and the girl helped the man find his way. The man said, "Thank you for helping me. I didn't know where to go."
The mom, the girl, and the man all smiled at each other. They were happy to have helped and talked with each other. And the girl learned that it's good to talk about things before we buy them, and it's nice to help others who don't know much.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big mirror in her room. Lily liked to look at herself in the mirror and make funny faces. One day, she saw a twist in her hair. She tried to fix it with her little hands.
Lily asked her mom for help. Her mom used a comb to untwist Lily's hair. They both looked at the mirror and laughed. Lily's hair was now nice and smooth. She was very happy.
In the room, there was a dead plant. Lily felt sad for the plant. She asked her mom if they could help it. Her mom said no, but they could get a new plant. So, they went to the store and bought a new, green plant. They put it next to the mirror, and Lily smiled.

Tom said, "Stop! I do not like the loud noise." The dogs did not stop. They kept playing. Tom felt mad. He wanted the dogs to stop.
Tom thought of a plan. He found a big bone and showed it to the dogs. The dogs stopped playing. They wanted the bone. Tom said, "I will give you the bone if you stop playing." The dogs agreed. They stopped playing, and Tom gave them the bone. Now, Tom could mail his letter in peace.

Charlie learned that day that not all eggs are good. He also learned that it is important to behave and listen to his mom. From that day on, Charlie always behaved and stayed away from spoiled eggs. And they all lived happily ever after.

Tom felt bad for making Lily cry. He took off the sweater and gave it to Lily. She put it on and smiled. They both learned that sharing made them happy. The beautiful sweater made them both feel good. And the moral is that sharing is caring.

"Mom, can I play with the ball?" Sally asked. "Be careful, Sally. Don't break the window," her mom said. Sally promised to be careful and started to play.
Sally kicked the ball high in the air. She tried to catch it, but she missed. The ball flew towards the window. Sally closed her eyes, scared that it would break. But, the ball hit the wall near the window and bounced away. Sally was happy that the window was safe. She decided to play with the ball far away from the window next time.

Once upon a time, there was a furry octopus named Ollie. Ollie lived in the big blue sea. He had many friends like fish, crabs, and turtles. Ollie loved to play with his friends all day.
One sunny day, Ollie and his friends wanted to start a fun game. They decided to play hide and seek. Ollie was very good at hiding because he could change colors to blend in. His friends were excited to play.
"Ready or not, here I come!" said Ollie's friend, Timmy the Turtle. Timmy swam around, looking for his friends. He found the fish behind a rock and the crab under the sand. But Ollie was very hard to find. Timmy looked and looked, but he could not find Ollie. Finally, Ollie changed back to his furry self and said, "Here I am, Timmy!" They all laughed and played more games until the sun went down.

On the train, Tim saw a big dog. The dog was loud too. Tim was scared of the dog. The dog's owner said, "Don't be scared, Tim. My dog is nice." Tim did not like the dog or the train.
At grandma's house, Tim told her about the train and the dog. Grandma said, "Next time, we will try something else. Maybe you will like it better." Tim was happy to be with grandma, away from the train and the dog.

Lucy wanted to see the big trucks up close, so she tried to walk closer to the road. But her mom held her hand tight and said, "No, Lucy, we need to stay away from the traffic. It's not safe." Lucy was sad, but she knew her mom was right. They walked home, and Lucy promised to be careful around the busy, wet road.
